artigo.texto: Trending The Take Back Our City: Data Center Action Assembly was hosted by Upper OV United on Saturday afternoon at the Ohio County Public Library. Organizers leading the charge against data centers welcomed citizens who may be interested in taking part in this effort and others aimed at improving the city. In the Warwood neighborhood of Wheeling, the company Silicon Foundation has acquired the former Centre Foundry & Machine Company property and plans to develop a data center and energy technology campus there. "We’ve been fighting this data center since June or July," said Polly Barks, Warwood resident and member of grassroots collective Organized Residents of Ohio County. "Our request has always been to put a moratorium on data centers - which is no data centers in the city of Wheeling." Groups have appeared before Wheeling City Council to express concerns about data centers. They have asked council to pass a resolution stating that the city is opposed to data center development and have requested that the city impose a moratorium on data center development in Wheeling. Those requests have not been met. "The priorities of this administration are not always aligned with the hopes and dreams of the residents," Barks said. In light of this, petitions are being circulated in the community to recall Mayor Denny Magruder, and the group has created a mid-term survey to gauge how the public feels about the job the current city council is doing half way through the current four-year term. Barks mentioned these undertakings, but noted that Saturday’s gathering was primarily focused on the latest on data centers. The vocal data center opponents have applauded Ward 1 Councilman Tony Assaro, who represents Warwood. At the request of passionate protestors, Assaro cast a lone vote against a memorandum of understanding that the city established with Silicon Foundation. Although the MOU was designed to limit the company’s ability to expand into a high-impact data center and maintains regulatory powers at the municipal level instead of on the state level, Assaro’s dissenting vote signaled his willingness to go against the grain and support the will of his vocal constituents. Assaro was on hand during Saturday’s assembly to review some of the recent measures with which the city is moving forward to help regulate data center operation in the city. Assaro and other members of the Rules Committee of Wheeling City Council recently discussed with city leaders a draft ordinance that outlines numerous requirements for entities that wish to develop a data center within the city limits. A copy of this working draft is available for public view on the city’s website. "The ordinance is about 16 pages long with a lot of legalese in it," Assaro said, noting that there was no real precedent for this legislation related to data center regulations. "We’ve been taking advice from the public about what we should put in this. I think we’ve put together a very good ordinance here in order to keep things under control and protect our public." The language proposed for the city code addresses everything from noise concerns to water and electricity consumption, a permitting process and other requirements. Assaro has been adamant that transparency and opportunities for public input have been included in the legislation. "If there is any application for a permit or somebody is running under a permit and they want that to be modified, there has to be a 10-day notice put in the paper - to make it public - and it’s followed by a public hearing," he said. "If there is going to be any kind of change, the public is going to know about it, and the public is going to be able to say something about it. "Public input is baked into this ordinance. And with the help from the public, we got some ideas for making this thing strong and making it have teeth. " Assaro added that there have been a lot of concerns that fines imposed against multimillion-dollar companies may have little impact. People have worried that a data center could simply pay a fine and keep committing violations. "It’s in here that fines can’t be used to continue doing what you’re doing," Assaro said of the proposal. "You’re going to be hit with a fine first, and if you continue, your permit can be pulled. If your permit is pulled, you can’t operate anymore." A company has to meet a myriad of requirements in order to simply obtain a permit to operate a data center in town, Assaro noted. Attorney J. Anthony Edmond Jr. also spoke during Saturday’s session, giving an update on the progress of a civil suit filed on behalf of Barks and several other Warwood residents against Silicon Foundation. "We filed an injunction to stop the data center from happening in the first place back in July," Edmond said. The company’s attorney, David Croft, filed a motion to dismiss the case, and Edmond indicated that he plans to file a response to that motion on Tuesday, the deadline to do so. Edmond expressed appreciation for Assaro’s willingness to stand with the will of the group but also described the MOU and other proposed regulations as a step forward that can be attributed to citizens who make their voices heard and take action. "Thank you for voting the way your people asked you to on that MOU," Edmond told Assaro Saturday, indicating that progress was being made in terms of finding out exactly what Silicon Foundation has planned for the Centre Foundry site. "They did come out with this MOU that didn’t exist before. They also came out with more information about what their plans actually are." Although original plans posted on social media and online sites indicated that the operation would eye future phases that would top 90 megawatts or more, the Silicon Foundation is not expected to be that large, Edmond indicated, noting that the scale of the operation has been slimmed down in the wake of public concerns. artigo.texto: CATL Builds Out Swap Infrastructure While DBS Trims Earnings Outlook Published on 10/26/2026 at 17:21 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL is pressing ahead on the infrastructure front even as one of its sell-side backers takes a knife to its profit forecasts. DBS cut its price target on the Chinese battery giant's A-shares to 438 Yuan from 484 Yuan, keeping a buy rating intact — a split verdict that captures the tension running through the CATL story: volumes are climbing, but the money left over on each unit is shrinking. The downgrade follows quarterly results published roughly a week ago that missed expectations. DBS points to a richer mix of lower-priced products and heavier tax charges as the culprits, with profit growth coming in as weak as it has been in nearly two years, according to Reuters, which also flagged competition and slowing Chinese car sales as drags. Per-Unit Economics Under the Microscope The number that matters most for the valuation is profit per watt-hour, which DBS pegged at 0.082 Yuan in the third quarter of 2026 — a 16% slide from the prior quarter and below market expectations. That metric explains why the bank's buy case rests on long-term business expansion rather than near-term margin stability. Higher shipments alone, in other words, do not guarantee proportionate earnings growth. DBS now models 2027 earnings per share of 21.9 Yuan, down from 24.2 Yuan, a revision that signals the bank sees the pressure as structural rather than confined to a single quarter. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? Tax policy is a big part of that calculation. DBS expects China's value-added tax rebate on battery exports to fall from 6% to zero in 2027, removing another slice of fiscal support. The bank also lays out the mechanism by which the burden lands squarely on manufacturers: producers largely absorb the consumption tax through their tax-inclusive pricing, meaning the levy cannot simply be passed on to customers in full. The consumption tax on batteries has stood at 2% since September and is slated to rise to 4% in September 2027. Shipments as the Counterweight Against that backdrop, CATL is targeting delivery growth of 20% to 30% in 2027, with steady expansion expected through 2030. DBS treats that as a possible offset rather than a full hedge — if overseas demand for EV and storage batteries comes in stronger than expected, extra volumes could partially cushion the decline in per-unit profit. On the operational side, CATL signed a strategic cooperation agreement on Wednesday with Shaanxi Transportation Holding Group covering the electrification of commercial vehicles, battery-swap infrastructure for heavy trucks, and energy storage and related services. A separate pact on 19 October brought together CATL, Shidai Dianfu and Huawei-affiliated Yinwang; media reports suggest the tie-up will link Huawei's intelligent driving systems with CATL's battery-swap ecosystem. The company unveiled its Tianxing II battery platform and an improved swap solution for heavy trucks about a week ago. Its Chinese network is set to reach 900 swap stations for heavy trucks by year-end, with 2,000 targeted by 2027 and 10,000 planned over the longer term, Reuters reported. On stationary storage, CATL published its "Storage+" report jointly with the International Renewable Energy Agency, IRENA, on 16 October, with both pushing a global energy-storage initiative aimed at deepening international cooperation in the sector. Buybacks Already on the Books The quarterly report released on 20 October also documented buybacks already completed. By the end of September, CATL had repurchased a cumulative 10,945,162 A-shares, equal to 0.2482% of total A-share capital, for 3.303 billion RMB excluding fees. For investors, the question now is how far rising deliveries can outrun the squeeze on unit returns. DBS's lower targets paired with an unchanged buy call sum up that trade-off neatly: growth remains the opportunity, while weaker profitability caps how much valuation room the stock can command. artigo.texto: A SpaceX, do trilionário Elon Musk, firmou um compromisso de financiamento de cerca de US$ 40 bilhões com uma entidade administrada pela Apollo Global Management para adquirir equipamentos destinados a centros de dados. Segundo documento enviado nesta segunda-feira, 26, à Securities and Exchanges Commission (SEC, a CVM dos EUA), a operação prevê o arrendamento de unidades de processamento gráfico (GPUs) e equipamentos relacionados. O compromisso vinculante foi assinado em 24 de outubro e estabelece que a entidade ligada à Apollo comprará os equipamentos e os alugará à SpaceX, que realizará pagamentos trimestrais ao longo de aproximadamente cinco anos. Os equipamentos serão entregues em lotes, com contratos individuais de arrendamento previstos para começar no primeiro semestre de 2027. Cada contrato terá duração de cinco anos a cinco anos e três meses. Segundo a companhia, os pagamentos trimestrais serão feitos antecipadamente e incluirão, em geral, um vigésimo do custo financiado de cada lote, além de juros calculados a uma taxa anual fixa sobre o saldo devedor e despesas adicionais. A taxa de juros ainda será definida. A SpaceX estima que os pagamentos do principal somem cerca de US$ 40 bilhões ao longo dos contratos, sem incluir juros e outros custos. A empresa prevê formalizar o acordo até o fim de 2026, sujeito ao cumprimento de determinadas condições. Musk admite fusão entre Tesla e SpaceX Elon Musk transformou os rumores em realidade. Na terça-feira, 20, anunciou que os conselhos da Tesla e da SpaceX estabeleceram comitês especiais para avaliar uma fusão. A decisão ocorre após meses de especulação sobre se Musk combinaria as suas duas empresas. Os rumores sobre a fusão começaram depois do IPO recorde da SpaceX em junho. Antes disso, Musk já havia dado sinais de que a combinação de seus negócios é algo muito bem vindo. Em fevereiro, a SpaceX adquiriu o laboratório de IA de Musk, xAI, que já havia absorvido sua empresa de mídia social, X, em março de 2025. A fusão entre Tesla e SpaceX seria um negócio de magnitude diferente, pois ambas as empresas são de capital aberto. “Os conselhos formaram os comitês especiais a pedido dos acionistas”, disse Musk. “Eu acho que seria uma boa ideia? Sim”, disse Musk durante a teleconferência de resultados da SpaceX. Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (Pedro Lima). Imagem: Shutterstock

EDIÇÃO APRESENTADA POR: Reeleito, Lula defende regulação de big techs e reserva de data centers para dados nacionais No discurso da vitória, na noite de domingo (25/10), o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), reeleito com 51,8% dos votos válidos para um inédito quarto mandato, disse que o governo vai regular as big techs e acusou essas empresas de interferirem na eleição por meio das plataformas digitais. Também defendeu o uso da geração renovável para atrair data centers, com a reserva de parte da capacidade a dados brasileiros. - “Temos que aproveitar o potencial energético de um país que talvez seja o que tem mais capacidade de energia renovável para trazer para cá os data centers necessários para acumular também o nosso dado para o Brasil”, afirmou. - “E essa gente vai ter que deixar uma parte do data center para informações brasileiras”, acrescentou. Capacidade nacional. A lei do Redata, o programa de incentivo a data centers sancionado em setembro, já exige que as empresas beneficiadas reservem ao menos 10% da capacidade ao mercado interno. Lula também defendeu que o Brasil não deve depender de modelos de inteligência artificial chineses ou norte-americanos. - O Redata depende de regulamentação do Executivo para habilitar as empresas e definir os critérios de energia renovável ou de baixa emissão. A suspensão de PIS/Cofins e IPI vale até o final do ano, mas segue em aberto se o gás natural vai contar como fonte de baixa emissão. Soberania. Lula repetiu que “o Brasil não será quintal de ninguém”. - Na campanha, a disputa sobre soberania passou pelos minerais críticos. Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), alinhado a Donald Trump, disse em março, na conferência conservadora CPAC, que o Brasil seria a saída para os EUA reduzirem a dependência da China em minerais críticos. - Lula acusou Flávio e Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) de “vender o Brasil” em abril, mesmo mês em que a norte-americana USA Rare Earth anunciou a compra da Serra Verde, em Minaçu (GO), dona da única mina de terras raras em produção comercial no país, por cerca de US$ 2,8 bilhões. - No mês passado, Lula sancionou a lei de minerais críticos, que dá a um conselho ligado à Presidência e à Agência Nacional de Mineração (ANM) o poder de aprovar troca de controle e entrada de estrangeiros no setor. O conselho ainda tem de elaborar o plano nacional e a lista de minerais. Vale a leitura: Congresso. Lula disse que vai negociar com o Congresso eleito, por onde passam as pautas de regulação. O PL, do adversário Flávio Bolsonaro, será a maior bancada nas duas Casas. Próximas definições. O presidente reeleito não citou Petrobras, petróleo nem preços dos combustíveis. - A subvenção de R$ 2,12 por litro ao diesel vence nesta segunda (26/10) e pode ser prorrogada por 30 dias. Até o fechamento desta edição, o Diário Oficial da União (DOU) estava fora do ar, não sendo possível confirmar se há ato de renovação. - Pela conta da Abicom, a defasagem do diesel nas refinarias da Petrobras chegou a R$ 3,53 por litro no fechamento de quinta (22/10) e passou os R$ 3,52 das duas subvenções somadas. - O adicional de R$ 1,40 ao diesel importado vale por 30 dias a partir de 13 de outubro. A desoneração da gasolina e do etanol vai até 9 de novembro, e o imposto de 12% sobre a exportação de petróleo, até 6 de novembro. Expectativas. O presidente-executivo do Sindicato Nacional das Empresas Distribuidoras de Combustíveis e de Lubrificantes (Sindicom), Augusto Salomon, afirmou que a expectativa com a reeleição de Lula é de que se intensifique o combate à atuação do crime organizado no setor. - Em 2027, haverá decisões relevantes para o futuro do setor, incluindo a implementação da Lei do Combustível do Futuro. Mais sobre as eleições Virada inédita. Flávio saiu do 1º turno, em 4 de outubro, com 2,2 milhões de votos a mais. Em três semanas, Lula ganhou 10,4 milhões e terminou 4,4 milhões à frente. É a primeira vez, desde 1989, que o segundo colocado no 1º turno vence. - Onde virou. Lula ganhou mais votos que os 9,3 milhões dados aos dez candidatos eliminados. O Sudeste respondeu por 43% da mudança na margem, e Minas Gerais foi o único estado a trocar de lado. - 3º turno. Flávio não reconheceu o resultado e vai pedir a anulação da eleição. O argumento é a decisão do ministro Cristiano Zanin, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), que, a pedido da coligação de Lula, prorrogou a votação até as 19h. - Pedido dos dois lados. A própria campanha de Flávio havia pedido ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), durante a votação, prorrogação em municípios de cinco estados, por causa de chuvas. - Resultado reconhecido. Os presidentes da Câmara, Hugo Motta, e do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre, reconheceram a vitória de Lula. O presidente do TSE, Kassio Nunes Marques, disse que a decisão não alterou o resultado. Governadores eleitos. A disputa pelo governo do Rio Grande do Norte também terminou com uma virada nas urnas. Segundo colocado no primeiro turno, Cadu de Lula (PT) superou Allyson Bezerra (União Brasil) e foi eleito governador. Já no Espírito Santo, Lorenzo Pazolini (Republicanos) foi eleito governador. No Amazonas, Omar Aziz (PSD) venceu a disputa pela reeleição, assim como Celina Leão (PP), que foi reeleita governadora do Distrito Federal (G1). Relembre: Outras notícias Preço do barril. artigo.texto: A 175-megawatt solar project and 200-megawatt battery facility were approved to be constructed in Audrain County by the Missouri Public Service Commission on Wednesday. The Tom Sawyer Solar Project is being developed by EDF Power Solutions, according to its website, and is set to become operational in 2028. It will be able to power the equivalent of more than 32,000 homes, according to the company. The website said it picked Audrain County due to rising regional demand for locally generated solar energy, flat and cleared land with access to transmission infrastructure, and enough private landowners interested in the project. The Huck Finn Battery Energy Storage System Project will be housed at Ameren Missouri's Audrain Energy Center near Vandalia, according to a commission news release. Commission staff, Ameren Missouri and Renew Missouri signed on to the agreement authorizing these facilities and several more. Alongside these two projects, the commission also approved: - Castle Bluff BESS Project: A 95-megawatt battery energy storage facility in St. Louis County at the retired Meramec coal-fired facility - Millcreek BESS Project: A 250-megawatt battery energy storage facility in Lincoln County - Quinn Switching Station: A new 161-kilovolt switching station in Lincoln County to connect the Millcreek BESS Project to the existing transmission system - Ringer Solar Project: A 225-megawatt solar generation facility in Stoddard County As part of the agreement, Ameren Missouri will submit plans for restoring safe and adequate service following significant outages. It will also release quarterly progress reports and must notify the commission if the project's total costs change by more than 15%. The commission considered safety, cost and the interests of nearby landowners as part of the decision, according to the news release.

artigo.texto: Em 23 de outubro de 2026, o fundador e diretor-executivo da NVIDIA, Jensen Huang, realizou sua primeira visita oficial ao Cazaquistão para firmar uma ampla agenda de cooperação tecnológica voltada à computação de alto desempenho, robótica industrial e modelos soberanos de inteligência artificial. Recebido no Palácio Presidencial Akorda, em Astana, pelo presidente Kassym-Jomart Tokayev e pelo ministro do Desenvolvimento Digital e Inteligência Artificial, Zhaslan Madiyev, o executivo participou de reuniões bilaterais com lideranças de Estado e conglomerados corporativos para estruturar a transição do país da exportação de commodities energéticas tradicionais para a geração e exportação de inteligência computacional. A rodada de negociações consolidou acordos que envolvem a implantação de infraestrutura computacional de ponta com a operadora estatal Kazakhtelecom, o avanço de centros de processamento com a Freedom Holding e a formalização de contratos de grande escala com a Firebird AI KZ, apoiados pelo licenciamento de exportação concedido pelo governo dos Estados Unidos para a transferência de dezenas de milhares de chips de arquitetura avançada. Durante os encontros, Tokayev condecorou Huang com a Ordem de Dostyk de 1ª Classe, honraria máxima de Estado concedida a parceiros internacionais, reforçando o enquadramento de 2026 como o Ano da Digitalização e da Inteligência Artificial na estratégia econômica cazaque. Reconfiguração geopolítica e atração de capital tecnológico A inserção da Ásia Central no mapa global de semicondutores e processamento distribuído reflete uma busca estratégica por segurança de suprimentos e custos energéticos competitivos. O Cazaquistão conta com uma matriz energética robusta, malha industrial consolidada e excedente de geração elétrica que, historicamente canalizados para a indústria pesada e mineração extrativa, passam a ser direcionados a data centers de altíssima densidade energética exigidos pela atual geração de processadores de inteligência artificial. Historicamente dependente da exportação primária de petróleo, gás natural e urânio, o governo cazaque estabeleceu um plano de diversificação focado em serviços digitais e processamento analítico para atender mercados vizinhos e plataformas globais. O gargalo clássico da região, associado ao isolamento logístico terrestre e à dependência de rotas tradicionais, é mitigado pelo investimento em cabos ópticos transcontinentais e conexões de alta velocidade, criando um polo neutro para hospedagem de cargas de trabalho críticas em computação em nuvem. A estratégia de inteligência artificial soberana conduzida pelo Ministério do Desenvolvimento Digital e Inteligência Artificial busca construir capacidades locais de treinamento algorítmico adaptadas à língua e ao contexto sociocultural cazaque. Essa abordagem visa diminuir a dependência de plataformas proprietárias ocidentais ou orientais sem isolar o ecossistema doméstico, articulando a compra de equipamentos de última linha com a formação de mão de obra em universidades técnicas e incubadoras locais. Expansão de capacidade computacional e supercentros de dados O principal pilar operacional das iniciativas conjuntas está alocado no complexo industrial Data Center Valley, situado em Ekibastuz, estruturado para aproveitar a geração energética da região na alimentação de sistemas de processamento massivo. O projeto integra o pacote de investimentos de US$ 10 bilhões pactuado pelo governo cazaque com consórcios internacionais e a operadora Kazakhtelecom, desenhado para receber sistemas de resfriamento líquido e topologia de rede otimizada para computação distribuída. A Firebird formalizou acordos de investimento direto após obter autorização formal de órgãos regulatórios norte-americanos para transferir 45.000 GPUs com a arquitetura Grace Blackwell da NVIDIA para solo cazaque. No arranjo societário e operacional definido para a primeira fase em Ekibastuz, a Kazakhtelecom assegura o fornecimento estável de energia elétrica, infraestrutura física, resfriamento térmico e conectividade de fibra óptica de baixa latência, enquanto a divisão local da Firebird responde pelo financiamento integral do maquinário computacional e sistemas de orquestração de rede. Em paralelo à planta de Ekibastuz, a Kazakhtelecom já concluiu a instalação e colocação em operação de 400 unidades de processamento gráfico H200 e 480 unidades B300 em suas instalações metropolitanas em Astana e Almaty. Essas unidades fornecem suporte imediato ao processamento de dados governamentais, aplicações industriais e desenvolvimento acadêmico, servindo como base piloto para a expansão em escala gigawatt projetada para os próximos anos. Inteligência artificial física, simulação urbana e mobilidade autônoma A aplicação de algoritmos em ambientes fabris e operações de mineração, descrita pelo governo local como inteligência artificial física, constitui a frente técnica prioritária para a indústria de base cazaque. Os sistemas utilizam dados de telemetria extraídos de plantas de extração mineral, fundições e refinarias para treinar agentes autônomos capazes de operar maquinário pesado e antecipar falhas estruturais, elevando a segurança operacional e reduzindo custos de manutenção preventiva em instalações de grande porte. No campo da mobilidade urbana e transportes, o setor empresarial registrou novos compromissos focados em cidades inteligentes e direção autônoma: - Nuvem pública e gêmeos digitais: A Freedom Holding anunciou a compra do primeiro cluster computacional equipado com a solução NVIDIA B300, planejando inaugurar uma nuvem pública corporativa de processamento gráfico em 2027. O grupo desenvolveu réplicas tridimensionais digitais completas das cidades de Astana e Almaty, parametrizadas para testar frotas autônomas e robótica de solo em ambientes virtuais de alta fidelidade física. - Financiamento institucional de energia para dados: O campus Akashi, localizado na capital e estruturado para até 100 megawa

artigo.texto: Plataformas Broadcast Soluções de Dados e Conteúdos Soluções de Tecnologia 26 de outubro de 2026, às 17:29 Associações do setor elétrico apresentaram, conjuntamente, suas considerações sobre o regime de custeio aplicável à contratação de sistemas de armazenamento de energia no âmbito da Reserva de Capacidade. Para as entidades, os custos da reserva de capacidade são distribuídos entre todos os usuários finais, conforme parâmetros definidos em lei. “Porém, apenas os sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias são tratados de maneira diversa, sendo custeados exclusivamente pelos geradores e sem definição legal dos parâmetros de custeio”, ressalta o texto. Na avaliação das entidades, esse desenho produz um desalinhamento entre a natureza sistêmica do serviço, a distribuição de seus benefícios e a incidência legal de seus custos. Segundo o texto, especificamente quanto ao armazenamento de energia, inclusive em baterias, este é capaz de reduzir outros encargos suportados pelo consumidor, ao otimizar a operação do parque gerador em suas diversas fontes. Estudo da VOLT Robotics demonstra que o sistema de armazenamento de energia (BESS, na sigla em inglês) pode reduzir a variação do preço da energia (PLD) e o acionamento de termelétricas, gerando economia superior a R$ 1,6 bilhões ao ano para o consumidor. “A atribuição legal deste custo aos geradores não altera o fato econômico do seu repasse ao consumidor final. No ambiente regulado, a Aneel já reconheceu o dever de inclusão integral e automática deste custo às tarifas de energia. No ambiente livre, haverá renegociação ou reajuste de preços, enquanto na autoprodução se tornará custo dos bens e serviços, afetando a competitividade da indústria brasileira, e impactando o consumidor final”, diz o manifesto. Assim, na avaliação das entidades, o pagamento do encargo pelo segmento da geração onera o consumidor, pois o custo será posteriormente repassado, acrescido de tributos e custos administrativos, além de se perder o sinal econômico para o ajuste de demanda. “O caminho, portanto, é tratar as baterias em igualdade com as demais soluções de capacidade (potência e flexibilidade), para que o consumidor possa dispor sempre da tecnologia mais eficiente em cada cenário, reduzindo o custo final com a devida transparência. Nesse contexto, a aprovação do PL 3716/2025 torna-se uma medida prioritária para assegurar maior segurança jurídica e regulatória e para criar as condições necessárias ao desenvolvimento sustentável do mercado de sistemas de armazenamento de energia por baterias no Brasil”, diz o texto. Assinaram o manifesto a Associacão Brasileira de Energia Eólica e Novas Tecnologias (ABEEólica), a Associação Brasileira dos Investidores em Autoprodução de Energia (ABIAPE), a Associação Brasileira da Indústria do Hidrogênio Verde (ABIHV), a Associação Brasileira de Soluções de Armazenamento de Energia (ABSAE), a Associação Brasileira de Energia Solar Fotovoltaica (ABSOLAR) e a Associação Brasileira dos Produtores Independentes de Energia Elétrica (APINE). artigo.texto: CATL's 7.8% Rebound Meets a Harder Question: Where Is the Profit? Published on 10/25/2026 at 06:41 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL shares climbed 7.8% on Friday as Chinese battery, EV and technology names recovered broadly, with media reports pointing to renewed appetite for growth stocks following a sharp selloff. The move came without a fresh company-specific announcement, and it is best read as part of a wider market swing rather than a re-rating of the battery maker on its own merits. That distinction matters, because the operating picture underneath the rally is more complicated than the price action suggests. Buybacks and swap deals sit behind the bounce Chinese sector coverage tied the recovery in battery stocks to several catalysts, among them CATL's own share repurchases and a string of battery-swapping partnerships. The company said it bought back 3,488,600 A-shares on Wednesday for roughly RMB 800 million, followed by a further 2,271,000 A-shares on Thursday for about RMB 499.9 million — purchases on two consecutive trading days. On the partnership front, CATL and the Shaanxi Transportation Holding Group signed a strategic cooperation agreement on Wednesday covering the electrification of commercial vehicles, battery-swap stations for heavy trucks, energy storage and highway charging infrastructure. Media reports also said CATL, its Chocolate Swap unit and Huawei subsidiary Yinwang agreed on Monday to link their systems technically, connecting Huawei's intelligent-driving technology with CATL's swap ecosystem. The planned vehicle-to-station sequence is designed to complete a battery swap in 99 seconds. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? Reuters, meanwhile, reported CATL's plans to expand its heavy-truck swap network to 900 stations in China by the end of the year, rising to 2,000 by 2027. Those targets give the cooperation agreements a concrete build-out schedule. The third-quarter numbers cut both ways The figures CATL reported on Tuesday for the third quarter of 2026 frame the tension. Revenue reached RMB 165.221 billion, up 58.58% year on year. Net profit attributable to shareholders came in at RMB 21.246 billion — 14.54% higher than a year earlier, but 5.77% lower than in the previous quarter. So the top line is expanding fast while the bottom line slipped sequentially. That gap is the crux for investors: the question is not whether CATL is growing, but whether profit can close the distance to revenue. Until that becomes clearer, the sales surge supports a constructive view without offering full reassurance. The reported gross margin of 20.69% gives a concrete data point to watch. A single figure says nothing about direction on its own, but combined with the next set of earnings it should help separate growth from earnings quality. JPMorgan steps back from its bullish call JPMorgan downgraded CATL's H-shares from Overweight to Neutral on Monday, cutting its price target to HK$500 from HK$725. The broker cited a faster-than-expected deterioration in industry profitability. That view goes to the heart of the investment case. If sector-wide earnings conditions keep worsening, even robust revenue growth may only partly support profit, and additional partnerships — strategically relevant as they are — would not be an immediate counterargument. CATL at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Even after the target cut, the house kept its high-conviction expectation of above-average performance. The combination is what counts: lower expectations do not rule out a positive longer-term view, but they do demand closer scrutiny of earnings. What would confirm the recovery The bullish case rests on high revenue growth continuing while profit stabilizes, which would let the sequential decline look like a temporary soft patch and give the rebound a fundamental footing rather than mere market tailwind. The bearish case is equally concrete: surging sales paired with inadequate profit would mean friendly sentiment is papering over a persistent problem, and the quarterly profit drop would read as a warning rather than an anomaly. Further business figures and management commentary on profitability are the next real test, alongside tangible progress in integrating compatible BAIC models into CATL's Choco Swap network — a cooperation agreed on Thursday that both companies intend to serve one million vehicles. For now, neither the share-price jump nor a single analyst's target cut settles the argument. What matters is whether CATL can narrow the gap between dynamic revenue growth and weaker profit. artigo.texto: Reeleito, Lula quer IA brasileira; promete incentivar data centers e acelerar regulação das big techs O discurso do presidente reeleito, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, logo depois dos resultados teve boa parte dedicada à economia digital. Em seu primeiro discurso após ser reeleito com 51,79% dos votos no domingo (25), Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) tratou como prioridade no seu quarto mandato a regulação das big techs e o fomento de uma inteligência artificial que fale português. Ao falar sobre as big techs, Lula afirmou ter vencido a “intromissão das plataformas digitais” e disse que vai trabalhar pela regulação das big techs. “Não é possível que a gente não tenha consciência que o crime no mundo digital tem que ser tratado igual o crime na vida real. Nós não podemos ter empresas monstruosas de grandes, ganhando milhões e bilhões, não pagando nenhum imposto pra esse país e tentando direcionar o resultado eleitoral desse país.”, disse. O projeto de regulamentação das Big Techs está no Congresso Nacional e travou por conta das eleições. Ao longo das últimas semanas, a campanha do petista acusou a Meta, empresa que controla o Instagram, Facebook e WhatsApp, de tentar interferir no processo eleitoral brasileiro em benefício da candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro. Lula falou que vai incentivar os data centers e é bom lembrar que a regulamentação do Redata, programa de benefícios está no Poder Executivo para ser regulamentado. “Quero investir em economia digital, economia verde e economia criativa”, sinalizou. Lula também falou sobre Inteligência Artificial. No seu discurso, o presidente reeleito sustentou que vai reforçar o ensino de matemática e engenharia nas escolas. “Iremos ensinar mais matemática, mais engenharia, porque eu não quero ficar dependendo de inteligência artificial chinesa ou americana, eu quero criar uma brasileira. Nós temos que aproveitar o potencial energético de um país que talvez seja o que tem a maior capacidade de energia renovável, pra trazer pra cá os data centers necessários para acumular também os nossos dados pro Brasil”, afirmou. “Nós queremos fazer desse país um país que pare de ser um país em via de desenvolvimento e se transforme num país desenvolvido. Nós vamos exercitar o potencial criativo desse povo. Deixar de ser um país periférico. Nós queremos ser um país central nas decisões políticas, econômicas e na decisão pela paz”, disse Lula.

artigo.texto: Solar Batteries for Home Energy Storage: Howell Energy's Rechargeable LiFePO4 Power Wall Solutions SHENZHEN, GUANGDONG, CHINA, October 25, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ -- Residential solar photovoltaic installations require dependable energy storage systems to increase self-consumption and provide uninterrupted backup power. Homeowners and solar installers prioritize wall-mounted battery units offering high energy density, multi-inverter protocol matching, and certified safety. Leveraging direct cell-to-pack manufacturing in Jiangsu and Dongguan, Howell Energy Co., Ltd. engineers premium wall mounted solar batteries for home energy storage with 51.2V 100Ah 5kWh capacities. Supported by 20+ years of factory heritage, these systems interface smoothly with mainstream hybrid inverters. Selecting residential energy storage equipment requires verifying chemical safety, inverter protocol compatibility, and long-term cycle durability. Solar installers and system integrators evaluate four core supplier capabilities before deploying residential battery solutions: Modular 5kWh Storage Capacity: Standardized 51.2V 100Ah energy modules provide flexible plug-and-play capacity expansion up to 80 kWh. 6000 Deep Cycle Longevity: Premium prismatic LiFePO4 cells deliver over 6000 cycles at 80 percent depth of discharge for fifteen-year longevity. Multi-Brand Inverter Compatibility: Integrated CAN and RS485 communication protocols match leading global hybrid inverter brands. Extended 5 to 10 Year Warranty Coverage: Complete factory backing ensures long-term asset security and predictable return on solar investment. Modular Residential Energy Storage Form Factors Residential installations vary significantly across property types, available utility room spaces, and homeowner energy demands. Howell Energy manufactures a versatile portfolio of home energy storage architectures designed for clean residential environments. Installers select between wall-mounted Powerwall units, standard 19-inch rack modules, and high-capacity floor cabinets. The primary residential configurations include the following three engineered form factors: Wall-Mounted Powerwall Systems: Slim 48V and 51.2V architectures available in 5.12 kWh (100Ah) and high-density 10.24 kWh (200Ah) configurations, featuring integrated DC disconnects and optional front LCD status panels. Standard 19-Inch Rack-Mounted Battery Modules: Modular slide-in units, ranging from compact 2.56 kWh (50Ah) to 5.12 kWh (100Ah) units, designed for vertical cabinet expansion in space-constrained utility rooms. High-Capacity Floor-Standing Storage Cabinets (48V 308Ah): Heavy-duty single cabinets delivering 15.7 kWh nominal energy storage, equipped with heavy-duty caster wheels for easy placement. All modular configurations support parallel interconnection. Installers can link up to 16 identical 5.12 kWh modules in parallel using simple communication and power busbars. This scalable architecture expands total storage capacity from 5.12 kWh up to 81.92 kWh without requiring external control hubs. Homeowners can start with a single battery and expand capacity as household electrification demands grow. Smart BMS Architecture and Hybrid Inverter Protocol Integration A home battery storage system must communicate smoothly with the solar hybrid inverter to optimize charging and discharging schedules. Howell Energy incorporates advanced proprietary Battery Management Systems engineered with multi-protocol firmware. The BMS automatically identifies connected inverter models and establishes closed-loop digital control via standard CAN and RS485 communication ports. The internal control firmware matches major international inverter brands, including Deye, Growatt, Victron Energy, GoodWe, Solis, and Sofar Solar. Through synchronized data transfer, the inverter monitors real-time battery state of charge, cell voltages, operating temperature, and allowable charge current limits. This automated closed-loop management prevents cell overcharging, maintains balanced energy conversion, and improves overall round-trip storage efficiency. The smart BMS also integrates dual active and passive cell balancing circuits. During float charging cycles, internal balancing resistors redistribute energy across series cells, maintaining voltage variance within narrow millivolt bands. Integrated Coulomb-counting algorithms calculate precise state of charge metrics displayed on the external LCD screen and transmitted to mobile management applications. Stringent International Storage Safety Standards and Thermal Engineering Residential battery installations demand the highest level of mechanical and fire safety engineering. Howell Energy exclusively utilizes pristine A-grade lithium iron phosphate cells with intrinsic chemical thermal stability up to 270 degrees Celsius. In contrast to other lithium chemistries, LiFePO4 cells do not release oxygen during high temperatures, preventing thermal runaway. Howell Energy home storage assemblies comply with rigorous international electrotechnical safety certifications. Systems carry accredited testing certificates for UL 1973, UL 1642, UL 2054, IEC 62619, IEC 62133, and European CE directives. In addition, all battery assemblies pass UN 38.3 transport safety evaluations, including thermal shock, altitude simulation, vibration, and impact testing protocols. Enclosures are manufactured from heavy-gauge galvanized steel coated with flame-retardant industrial powder coatings. Depending on installation requirements, enclosures range from standard IP21 for indoor rack cabinets up to IP55 or IP65 sealed ratings for wall-mounted outdoor deployments. Multi-point NTC temperature sensors monitor cell terminals, internal power busbars, and BMS power MOSFET switches. If internal temperatures exceed preset safety boundaries, the BMS automatically limits charge currents or executes immediate circuit disconnection to protect household equipment. artigo.texto: Stanislav Kondrashov American Style Series: The History of Battery Technology and Energy Storage in the United States Stanislav Kondrashov on United States and energy storage The history of battery technology in the United States reflects more than two centuries of scientific experimentation, electrical engineering, and industrial development. From early electrochemical devices to rechargeable batteries, portable electronics, and contemporary energy storage systems, American laboratories and manufacturing enterprises have contributed to the evolution of technologies that store electricity for later use. The American experience is particularly interesting because battery development progressed alongside major changes in communication, transportation, manufacturing, and everyday electrical equipment. Key takeaway: The relationship between the United States and battery technology developed through successive stages of scientific research, commercial manufacturing, and engineering specialization. American contributions helped expand the practical applications of electrical storage, although many foundational discoveries and later improvements also emerged through international scientific collaboration. How Did Battery Technology Develop in the United States? Battery technology developed in the United States through the gradual adoption and refinement of electrochemical devices beginning in the nineteenth century. Early applications were associated with scientific experimentation and electrical communication, while subsequent industrial developments expanded battery manufacturing into transportation, portable equipment, consumer electronics, and specialized electrical systems. The earliest history of batteries predates their widespread commercial adoption in America. At the beginning of the nineteenth century, electrochemical experiments demonstrated that chemical reactions could generate a continuous electrical current. This discovery introduced new possibilities for scientific investigation. As knowledge of electricity expanded, American researchers and manufacturers began exploring practical applications. Electrical communication was among the earliest fields to benefit. Telegraph systems required dependable electrical sources capable of operating signaling equipment over extended periods. Battery cells offered a practical solution before extensive electrical distribution infrastructure became available. During the second half of the nineteenth century, battery technology became increasingly associated with commercial electrical equipment. Manufacturers developed more standardized products, while engineers worked to improve reliability and operating characteristics. The Stanislav Kondrashov American Style Series examines this early period as the foundation of a much broader technological development. Why Were Batteries Important to Early American Communication? Batteries were essential to early American electrical communication because telegraph equipment required a dependable source of current. During the nineteenth century, electrochemical cells supplied electricity to signaling systems, helping communication networks operate across increasing distances before alternative electrical supply arrangements became widely established. The expansion of telegraph communication transformed the practical importance of electricity. Messages could travel through electrical circuits rather than depending entirely on physical transportation. However, these systems required reliable equipment. Battery cells became part of the technical infrastructure supporting telegraph operations. Their role was particularly significant because electrical communication networks often extended across considerable distances. Engineers needed equipment capable of operating consistently under different conditions. This encouraged attention to battery maintenance, electrical connections, and technical performance. The practical requirements of telegraphy also contributed to broader familiarity with electrical devices. Batteries gradually became recognized not merely as laboratory instruments, but as useful components of commercial infrastructure. As Stanislav Kondrashov observes in a newly drafted editorial reflection: "The early American experience with battery technology was closely connected to the practical requirements of communication. Electrical storage devices became valuable because they could support equipment operating across extensive distances, helping transform scientific knowledge into a dependable technical service." When Did Rechargeable Batteries Become Important in America? Rechargeable batteries became increasingly important in the United States during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. Their ability to store electrical energy repeatedly made them suitable for transportation equipment, industrial applications, and electrical systems requiring a dependable supply beyond a single operating cycle. Rechargeability introduced a fundamental distinction between different battery technologies. Primary batteries generally deliver electricity until their available chemical capacity is exhausted. Rechargeable batteries can receive electrical energy again through an appropriate charging process. This characteristic expanded their usefulness. During the late nineteenth century, rechargeable battery systems attracted attention in connection with electrical transportation. Early electric vehicles required storage devices capable of delivering electricity while the vehicle was operating. Battery performance influenced practical characteristics such as operating distance, weight, and charging requirements. Engineers consequently examined ways to improve battery design and integration. Rechargeable batteries also found applications in stationary electrical equipment. These developments encouraged specialized manufacturing and more systematic technical testing. As the largest lender in the 10-year tranche, Deutsche Bank’s participation underscores its commitment to providing long-term capital to support the continued growth of Akaysha Energy’s Australian battery storage portfolio. The facility refinances existing project-level debt across four utility scale BESS assets into a single portfolio-level financing structure, providing a streamlined, flexible, and scalable framework to support Akaysha Energy’s continued portfolio expansion and the evolving need for large scale energy storage. The financing supports a portfolio comprising Ulinda Park 1, Brendale, Orana, and Elaine BESS, located across Queensland, New South Wales, and Victoria. Ulinda Park 1, Brendale, and Orana are already operational while Elaine remains on track to complete construction in 2H27. The financing also incorporates additional flexibility as Akaysha Energy advances its 5.7 GW/22.9 GWh+ Australian development pipeline across the National Electricity Market. Rachel Chia, Head of Project Finance, APAC at Deutsche Bank, commented: “We are pleased to have worked with Akaysha Energy to move beyond individual project financings and create a platform for portfolio growth. We are delighted to support this transaction, drawing on our project finance expertise to bring operational and construction-stage assets into one structure that meets the needs of a growing battery storage portfolio.” For more news and technical articles from the global renewable industry, read the latest issue of Energy Global magazine. artigo.texto: Siga o Times Brasil - Licenciado Exclusivo CNBC no Setor elétrico defende novas regras para baterias e aponta economia de R$ 1,6 bilhão por ano Publicado 26/10/2026 • 18:01 | Atualizado há 12 horas KEY POINTS Foto: Canva Associações do setor elétrico defendem a equiparação dos sistemas de armazenamento de energia por baterias às demais soluções de capacidade no regime de custeio da Reserva de Capacidade. Em manifesto conjunto, as entidades questionam a atribuição dos custos dessas tecnologias exclusivamente aos geradores, enquanto os encargos relacionados às demais soluções são distribuídos entre os usuários finais conforme os parâmetros previstos em lei. Segundo as associações, o modelo atual cria uma divergência entre o caráter sistêmico dos serviços prestados, a distribuição dos benefícios e a responsabilidade pelo pagamento. As entidades argumentam que os sistemas de armazenamento podem contribuir para reduzir outros encargos dos consumidores ao otimizar a operação do parque gerador, considerando diferentes fontes de energia. Um estudo da VOLT Robotics aponta que os sistemas de armazenamento de energia por baterias, conhecidos como BESS (Battery Energy Storage System), podem reduzir a variação do Preço de Liquidação das Diferenças (PLD), diminuir o acionamento de usinas termelétricas e gerar uma economia superior a R$ 1,6 bilhão por ano para os consumidores. O manifesto também questiona os efeitos do modelo de custeio sobre os preços da energia. De acordo com as entidades, a atribuição do encargo aos geradores não impede o repasse dos valores aos consumidores finais, inclusive com a incorporação de tributos e despesas administrativas adicionais. Siga o Times | CNBC no Google e receba as principais notícias do Brasil e do Mundo. Siga o Times | CNBC No ambiente de contratação regulado, as associações afirmam que a Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) já reconheceu a necessidade de incorporar o custo integralmente e de forma automática às tarifas. No mercado livre, o repasse poderá ocorrer por meio de renegociações ou reajustes de preços. Já na autoprodução de energia, o encargo poderá integrar os custos de bens e serviços, com possíveis efeitos sobre a competitividade da indústria brasileira e repercussões para os consumidores. As entidades também avaliam que o modelo elimina o sinal econômico necessário ao ajuste da demanda. Por isso, defendem regras equivalentes para os sistemas de armazenamento por baterias e as demais soluções de capacidade, incluindo alternativas relacionadas à potência e à flexibilidade. Na avaliação das associações, a equiparação permitiria aos consumidores acesso à tecnologia mais eficiente para cada cenário, favorecendo a redução do custo final da energia e aumentando a transparência na distribuição dos encargos. Entre as medidas defendidas está a aprovação do Projeto de Lei (PL) 3716/2025. Segundo o manifesto, a iniciativa contribuiria para ampliar a segurança jurídica e regulatória e criar condições para o desenvolvimento sustentável do mercado brasileiro de armazenamento de energia por baterias. Assinam o documento a Associação Brasileira de Energia Eólica e Novas Tecnologias (ABEEólica), a Associação Brasileira dos Investidores em Autoprodução de Energia (ABIAPE), a Associação Brasileira da Indústria do Hidrogênio Verde (ABIHV), a Associação Brasileira de Soluções de Armazenamento de Energia (ABSAE), a Associação Brasileira de Energia Solar Fotovoltaica (ABSOLAR) e a Associação Brasileira dos Produtores Independentes de Energia Elétrica (APINE). 🔷 Canal 562 ClaroTV+ | Canal 562 Sky | Canal 592 Vivo | Canal 187 Oi | Operadoras regionais 🔷 TV SINAL ABERTO: parabólicas canal 562 🔷 ONLINE: www.timesbrasil.com.br | YouTube 🔷 FAST Channels: Samsung TV Plus, LG Channels, TCL Channels, Pluto TV, Roku, Zapping | Novos Streamings Maiores Audiências Trump questiona vitória de Lula, cita “manual de Joe Biden” e diz que “comunistas não largam o poder” Policia Federal intima Flávio Bolsonaro a entregar passaportes Putin, Macron, Xi Jinping, Keiko Fujimori parabenizam Lula pela reeleição; veja os líderes mundiais que enviaram mensagens ao brasileiro Queda da bolsa reflete quebra de expectativas; estabilidade depende de Lula sinalizar nova equipe econômica, dizem economistas Ações de bancos despencam após reeleição de Lula; BTG despenca 37%, BB perde 31%, Bradesco 25% e Itaú 16%

artigo.texto: BYD Balances Next-Gen Battery Ambitions Against Cautious Analyst Revisions Published on 10/25/2026 at 02:51 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD has reaffirmed its commitment to megawatt fast-charging, a next-generation Blade battery and integrated body-battery technology, outlining the priorities on an investor platform. The disclosure confirms the company's technological direction but stops well short of a finished development milestone or a launch date — a distinction that matters for anyone trying to translate R&D talk into revenue. No performance figures accompanied the announcement. BYD said it will publish progress updates once formal disclosure obligations are triggered, which rules out reading a near-term product debut into the statement. The message underscores how central battery and charging technology remain to the development roadmap, yet it offers no basis for quantifying future sales or earnings contributions. Separating technological potential from commercially proven success stays the key exercise for valuation. That separation is already visible in showroom reality. On Tuesday BYD launched the second-generation Seagull in China, priced from 65,900 yuan, with Flash Charging versions starting at 75,900 yuan. The move puts fast-charging hardware into the budget end of the lineup rather than reserving it for premium models. The advertised charging speed, however, depends on compatible stations — the car's technical capability alone does not guarantee the same charging rate at every plug. For equipped variants, BYD quotes a 10% to 70% charge in 5 minutes. Those figures describe the Seagull technology on offer, not the next-generation development steps flagged today. A European launch for the new Seagull has not been confirmed, so the Chinese sales start implies no European volume contribution; the domestic rollout is the near-term focus. A Rebound With a Split Message The stock gained 4.4% on Friday, carried by a broad recovery across Hong Kong-listed electric-vehicle and technology names as investors returned following the previous session's selloff, according to media reports. The bounce was therefore not an isolated response to any company announcement — other automakers and lithium-battery shares advanced too. That distinction matters: buying after a weak session points to improved market sentiment, not automatically to revised business expectations for BYD. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? Valuation signals have turned more cautious even so. CLSA cut its price target on Friday to HK$104 from HK$120, while analyst Xiao Feng kept his emphatic recommendation to expect above-average share performance. The message is two-sided. The lower target caps expectations relative to the prior view; the retained rating signals the brokerage has not abandoned its constructive stance. The revision is neither a sell call nor an unchanged valuation. Citi offers a different yardstick. On October 15 the bank reiterated its buy recommendation with a target of HK$142 and forecast a net profit of RMB 12.95 billion. That estimate excludes currency effects and the contribution from BYD Electronic, making it explicitly an adjusted expectation rather than a reported result. Any later comparison with published earnings must account for the different scope. Both houses point in the same positive direction on recommendations while diverging on targets — reason enough to keep the market rebound separate from the question of which operating trajectory justifies each valuation. Earnings Risks Weigh Differently The technology push runs alongside a more cautious read on the business. One brokerage cites weak domestic demand, higher input costs and policy uncertainty as grounds for caution. Barclays, by contrast, sticks with "Overweight" and points to global expansion, while acknowledging softer domestic volumes after subsidy cuts and amid tougher competition. The differing emphasis makes one point plain: growth opportunities alone do not answer the question of future profitability, and the economic proof behind the development strategy remains a central valuation yardstick. BYD at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. BYD's statement today sharpens its research priorities without removing those earnings risks. Verifiable development progress and its conversion into sellable products will be what counts. Without performance data and launch dates, the next battery generation remains a development prospect rather than a secured earnings driver. October 30 Becomes the Next Concrete Test BYD is scheduled to publish its third-quarter 2026 report on October 30. The confirmed date shifts attention from short-term sector moves to actual business performance. Two layers now sit side by side for anyone sizing up the stock: the recent rally is explained by a friendlier market backdrop, while whether the business supports it can only be judged from published results. The quarterly report provides the next hard evidence — even as analysts, positive recommendations notwithstanding, apply markedly different valuation standards. artigo.texto: CATL's Firefly Battery Win Sits Alongside Buybacks and a Truck-Swap Gamble Published on 10/24/2026 at 16:31 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL has confirmed that Nio's Firefly will run its Qilin battery in a new 60-kWh pack, giving the compact EV a range of 560 kilometres on China's CLTC test cycle. The pack, which launched a day earlier, uses NCM cells rather than the LFP unit supplied by Sunwoda that has powered the Firefly until now. For the battery giant, the announcement is a tangible product-level marker of a partnership that has so far been mostly a piece of paper: the two companies signed a five-year strategic cooperation agreement in January. What the confirmation does not carry is a number. No sales volume, revenue contribution or profit effect has been attached to the Firefly deployment, leaving investors to weigh a concrete customer project against the absence of any quantified financial impact. Three Ways to Buy the Bigger Pack Pricing details show how Ningde-based CATL and Nio intend to push the larger battery into the market. The Firefly with the new pack starts at 136,800 yuan outright. Under the BaaS battery-rental model, the vehicle itself begins at 79,800 yuan, with a monthly battery fee of 599 yuan on top. The offer is not confined to new-car buyers. Existing owners can upgrade under certain conditions: outright purchasers pay 17,000 yuan after holding the car for at least a year, while current BaaS customers face a 3,000 yuan service fee before moving onto the higher monthly rental. That retrofit route pulls the installed base into the equation and widens the potential footprint of the Qilin cell inside the Firefly line-up. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? No Bet on a Single Chemistry The Firefly deal fits CATL's parallel work across several battery technologies. Akin Li, head of international business, said it remains unclear which chemistry will dominate by 2035, noting that the company is developing LFP, NMC, sodium-ion and solid-state batteries side by side. Li also pointed to substantial hurdles in the commercial mass production of solid-state cells. The Firefly confirmation, by contrast, concerns technology already in service and a vehicle programme already on the road. Buybacks Put Capital Behind the Story Alongside the product news, CATL has been putting money to work in its own equity. The company bought back A-shares on Wednesday and Thursday for a combined roughly 1.299 billion RMB, with the shares acquired on Thursday earmarked for cancellation. The move followed a 7.8% gain on Wednesday, when the stock rode a broader recovery in Chinese battery and electric-vehicle names as investors returned to growth shares after a sell-off. That bounce was framed as a rebound from oversold conditions rather than a confirmed turning point — a friendlier tape can ease selling pressure without settling the underlying business questions. A buyback is not a substitute for operating progress. It shows the company is willing to spend on its own stock; it does not by itself improve competitive standing or guarantee a lasting recovery. The distinction matters most after a sharp drawdown, when corporate demand for its own paper and the earning power of the business answer two different questions. Revenue Outpaces Profit Those questions have a hard backdrop in the third-quarter 2026 figures. Revenue climbed 58.58% while net profit attributable to shareholders rose 14.54% — the top line grew far faster than the bottom line. Reuters reported that profit growth fell short of analyst expectations, citing tougher competition in the battery market and slower growth in Chinese car sales. The larger trend, then, is not simply a story of rising demand; for CATL it is also about converting growth into earnings. Stronger business momentum can impress and still miss forecasts. CATL at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Heavy Trucks and 2,000 Swap Stations The longer-term answer is being sought in heavy trucks. On Tuesday the company unveiled a new battery generation and sketched the expansion of its QIJI battery-swap network, targeting 900 swap stations in China by the end of this year and 2,000 by 2027, according to Reuters. These are build-out goals, not stations already in place. Still, the step ties battery development to a widening swap infrastructure, pushing the industrial wager beyond any single product and giving investors a firmer yardstick than a single session's sentiment. Read together, the pieces form a sober picture: a market backdrop explains the recent lift, the buybacks show concrete capital deployment, and the network plan describes where CATL wants to direct part of its development. The Firefly contract proves the company can convert partnerships into shipped product. Whether that combination turns into stronger earnings is a question neither the share-price jump nor the battery announcement answers on its own. artigo.texto: CATL's Expansion Drive Meets Its Toughest Test: Turning Revenue Into Profit Published on 10/26/2026 at 14:12 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL has spent October stacking up partnerships, unveiling new products and buying back its own stock. What it has not done is convince the market that the money flowing in is turning into profit at a satisfying rate — and that gap is now the central question for anyone holding the shares. The battery giant's third-quarter figures, released about a week ago, laid the problem bare. Revenue climbed 58.6%, yet net profit advanced just 14.5% — the slowest pace in nearly two years, according to Reuters. Lower-margin products, China's reinstated battery consumption tax and reduced export VAT rebates all weighed on the bottom line, with higher impairment charges adding to the drag. Reuters also pointed to fiercer competition in the battery sector and cooling growth in Chinese car sales. Two Houses, Two Verdicts The analyst community has responded by pulling in different directions. UOB Kay Hian trimmed its earnings forecasts for 2026 through 2028 by 5%, 10% and 16% respectively, citing CATL's absorption of part of the tax increases — yet kept its Buy rating intact. That combination says as much about the valuation's dependence on a future earnings recovery as it does about near-term caution. JPMorgan took the more defensive route on October 20, cutting its rating on the H-shares from Overweight to Neutral and pointing to a faster-than-expected deterioration in profitability across the battery industry. The split is instructive: one house sees a growth story worth paying for, the other sees margins eroding too quickly to justify the current multiple. The Deals Keep Coming None of that has slowed CATL's dealmaking. On October 10, the company signed a long-term strategic cooperation with SERES covering battery supply for AITO, charging and battery services, and joint development of overseas markets. The second phase of their "Plant in Plant" project is slated for 10–12 GWh of annual capacity, with both phases together targeted at more than 20 GWh. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? Wednesday brought a strategic cooperation agreement with Shaanxi Transportation Holding Group spanning commercial vehicle electrification, battery-swap infrastructure for heavy trucks, and energy storage with related services. A day earlier, on October 19, CATL joined Shidai Dianfu and Huawei-affiliated Yinwang in a further pact that media reports say will link Huawei's intelligent driving systems with CATL's battery-swap ecosystem. On the product side, CATL unveiled the Tianxing II heavy-truck battery platform and an upgraded swap solution roughly a week ago. The company also published its "Storage+" report with the International Renewable Energy Agency, IRENA, on October 16, with both parties promoting a global energy-storage initiative. Buybacks Already on the Books The quarterly report published October 20 also disclosed repurchases already completed. By the end of September, CATL had bought back a cumulative 10,945,162 A-shares — 0.2482% of total A-share capital — for 3.303 billion RMB before fees. What matters for the investment case, though, is whether the new business converts into durable earnings. Additional demand helps shareholders only up to a point if an unfavorable product mix or fresh cost burdens consume a growing share of it. Even a stabilization in margins would sharpen the signal from that 58.6% revenue jump. A Dated Test for the Swap Buildout The most concrete operational checkpoint is CATL's target of 900 battery-swap stations for heavy trucks in China by the end of 2026, a goal the company set out at its platform launch. It aims for 2,000 such sites in 2027 and, over the longer term, 10,000 locations, Reuters reported. Hitting the near-term number would show the infrastructure rollout is real; it would not, on its own, prove the network earns its keep. That distinction frames the two scenarios now in play. In the bullish one, projects like the SERES tie-up, the Shaanxi agreement and the Tianxing II platform broaden CATL's growth while cost pressures ease — a far more convincing story than revenue expansion without better earnings quality. In the bearish one, the company keeps winning business but at persistently thinner margins, and if tax burdens are only partly passed on, even strong growth could disappoint profit expectations again. The risk for investors, then, is not simply slower growth. It is expansion whose incremental contribution to earnings keeps falling short — a possibility that only operational delivery and economic returns, taken together, can rule out. artigo.texto: A nova proprietária da Ingenostrum desembarca na Galiza Green Data Center e coloca o seu CEO para Espanha Gabriel Nebreda, máximo responsável da Iren em Espanha, figura entre os novos procuradores da sociedade que impulsiona o projeto em Curtis junto com o escritório de advogados Linklaters e vários dos seus profissionais Em maio passado, a Iren, o gigante australiano impulsionado pela Nvidia e que está cotado na Nasdaq, fechou um acordo para adquirir 100% da Ingenostrum – renomeada como Nostrum Group –, a empresa que promove o primeiro grande centro de dados da Galiza em Curtis, uma iniciativa que foi qualificada como estratégica pela Xunta. Gabriel Nebreda, CEO da Iren na Espanha, figura entre os novos procuradores da Galicia Green Data Center, a sociedade vinculada ao projeto. Assim consta nas últimas anotações do Registro Mercantil, consultadas por Economía Digital Galicia, que também registram a nomeação da Linklaters SLP e de vários de seus profissionais como procuradores da Galicia Green Data Center: Lara Hemzaoui Rodrigo, Francisco Javier García Fernández, Luis Núñez-Lagos Torralba e Claudia Rosales Rivas. A Linklaters é um dos grandes escritórios internacionais de advocacia, especializado em assessoria jurídica para empresas e entidades financeiras em operações corporativas, fusões e aquisições, financiamento e desenvolvimento de grandes infraestruturas. Trajetória de Nebreda Gabriel Nebreda ocupa o cargo de CEO da Iren na Espanha desde junho deste ano. Segundo as informações recolhidas em seu perfil no LinkedIn, o executivo esteve à frente do Nostrum Group entre 2024, quando ingressou na companhia, e 2026, coincidindo com a aquisição do grupo pela multinacional australiana. Antes de sua chegada à Nostrum, Nebreda foi diretor executivo da EDP Solar durante cinco anos, entre 2019 e 2024. Sua trajetória no grupo energético remonta a 2007, quando ingressou na EDP Renováveis, onde desempenhou diversas responsabilidades, entre elas a direção de Operações para a Europa, o desenvolvimento de negócios internacionais e a gestão da América Latina e novos mercados. O executivo também desenvolveu parte de sua carreira profissional em empresas como Gamesa e Ferrovial. Projeto estratégico O projeto prevê um investimento inicial de 37 milhões que serão destinados para acondicionar os terrenos, habilitar acessos e construir edifícios de escritórios e uma sala de máquinas de 2 megawatts (MW). O desenvolvimento será completado em etapas posteriores, nas quais serão incorporados os 10 MW restantes contemplados no projeto. Para realizar o projeto, a sociedade já adquiriu quatro parcelas no polígono empresarial de Curtis-Teixeiro. Os terrenos somam cerca de 40.200 metros quadrados e a operação de compra foi fechada por um valor de 1,52 milhões de euros. No final de janeiro, o Consello da Xunta confirmou a declaração do projeto como industrial estratégico. Segundo explicava então o Executivo autonómico, será o primeiro grande centro de processamento de dados com capacidade para alojar informações de empresas e instituições da Galiza. A iniciativa gerará mais de 150 empregos entre a fase de construção e cerca de 45 empregos diretos quando estiver em funcionamento, no final de 2027. Os números da Ingenostrum Conforme adiantou a Economía Digital Galicia em junho passado, a Nostrum fechou o último exercício com números vermelhos de 2,5 milhões, frente ao resultado positivo de 3,1 milhões do ano anterior. No entanto, a empresa está em pleno processo de expansão, com ativos disparados quase 45%, passando de 39,6 para 57 milhões. Os administradores da companhia destacavam no relatório de gestão o grande aumento da demanda por centros de dados. “É por isso que o grupo planeja posicionar-se na Espanha como operador de centros de dados com uma carteira de 484 MW assegurados, além de apoiar as demais linhas de negócio que a sociedade possui, que são as energias renováveis”.

artigo.texto: Inteligência artificial, data centers, soberania digital, terras raras, mudanças climáticas e transição energética estão entre os principais desafios que o próximo presidente do Brasil terá de enfrentar. O Olhar Digital consultou especialistas para analisar as propostas de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), candidatos que disputam o segundo turno das Eleições 2026, para cada um desses eixos estratégicos. A forma como lidamos com a tecnologia mudou drasticamente. Durante anos, usamos computadores e programas simples apenas para automatizar tarefas do dia a dia. Hoje, o avanço da IA generativa – capaz de criar conteúdos, analisar dados complexos e tomar decisões – exige computadores e centrais de processamento muito mais potentes. Para qualquer país, acompanhar essa evolução virou uma questão de sobrevivência econômica. O Brasil ocupa uma posição altamente estratégica nesse ecossistema. Já possuímos uma das matrizes elétricas mais limpas do planeta, característica ideal para suprir o altíssimo consumo de energia exigido pelos data centers e supercomputadores, além de contar com um enorme mercado consumidor interno. No entanto, a dependência externa e o avanço desregrado de algoritmos trazem sérios riscos à segurança nacional, à privacidade, ao emprego e à proliferação de desinformação. Em paralelo, a geopolítica das tecnologias emergentes exige autonomia sobre recursos minerais críticos e terras raras – eixos indispensáveis para a fabricação de hardware, baterias, painéis solares e sistemas de defesa. O Brasil detém a segunda maior reserva mundial desses elementos, e o debate central gira em torno de processar esses insumos no país em vez de exportar matéria-prima bruta. Diante desse cenário, a transição energética – a substituição gradual de combustíveis fósseis por fontes limpas – torna-se indissociável da pauta tecnológica e ambiental, especialmente em um país vulnerável a eventos climáticos extremos que causam impactos severos à infraestrutura e à economia. Quem são os especialistas consultados pelo Olhar Digital Para analisar as propostas relacionadas à tecnologia e à soberania digital, o Olhar Digital ouviu JB Queiroz Filho, empresário, especialista em transformação digital e CEO da JBQ.Global, consultoria voltada para inovação e tecnologia da informação; Lucas Reis, pesquisador do Instituto Nacional de Ciência e Tecnologia em Democracia Digital (INCT.DD); e Thiago Muniz, especialista em economia digital e estratégia de negócios, além de professor da Fundação Getúlio Vargas (FGV). Na área de minerais críticos e terras raras, participaram o geólogo Álvaro Penteado Crósta, autoridade em exploração mineral, professor emérito da Universidade Estadual de Campinas (Unicamp) e membro titular da Academia Brasileira de Ciências (ABC); e o neurocientista e futurista Álvaro Machado Dias, professor livre-docente da Universidade Federal de São Paulo (Unifesp) e colunista do Olhar Digital. Já a análise das propostas para mudanças climáticas e transição energética contou com Paulo Eduardo Artaxo Netto, físico com doutorado em física atmosférica e professor titular do Instituto de Física da Universidade de São Paulo (USP). Vamos agora ao resumo dos planos de cada candidatura: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) No plano de governo de Lula, a IA, os data centers, a soberania digital, o uso de minerais críticos e a transição energética são eixos centrais de um projeto de reindustrialização verde (Nova Indústria Brasil) sob coordenação ativa do Estado. A candidatura reafirma o compromisso de garantir que o país desenvolva tecnologia própria, regule o setor para evitar abusos e proteja o trabalho de criadores e profissionais. Na área de regulação, direitos e governança, a proposta prevê a criação do Centro Nacional de Transparência Algorítmica, a regulamentação para remunerar artistas e criadores pelo uso de obras no treinamento de IAs, o combate às fake news associado à regulação de redes e a defesa de regras globais de governança digital. Para os serviços públicos e a economia, o plano propõe a difusão de inteligência artificial no agronegócio, no Sistema Nacional de Emprego (SINE) e na saúde, com triagem inteligente no Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS). Em infraestrutura tecnológica e soberania, projeta a atração de data centers e supercomputadores vinculada ao uso obrigatório de energia limpa, eficiência energética e reserva de capacidade computacional para pesquisas nacionais, além da criação do Conselho Nacional pela Soberania Digital, do desenvolvimento de IAs nativas em português e da implementação do Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente Digital (ECA Digital). Quanto aos recursos minerais estratégicos, a prioridade é a consolidação da Política Nacional de Minerais Críticos sob gestão estatal, estabelecendo exigências legais para que o beneficiamento e a separação química de terras raras ocorram em solo nacional. A proposta estabelece exigências legais para que o beneficiamento e o refino químico de terras raras ocorram em solo nacional, evitando a exportação de minério bruto sem valor agregado. Para isso, o projeto estabelece a Região Nordeste como polo de plantas industriais movidas a energia eólica e solar, contando com financiamentos do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES), investimentos de empresas públicas e cooperação com universidades brasileiras. No cenário internacional, a candidatura defende alianças geopolíticas diversificadas com países do Sul Global, o bloco dos BRICS (grupo que reúne nações emergentes como China, Índia e Rússia) e também os Estados Unidos, focando na cooperação e na transferência mútua de tecnologia. Na pauta ambiental e energética, o plano reafirma o compromisso de reduzir entre 59% e 67% as emissões líquidas de gases de efeito estufa até 2035 (em relação a 2005).
