artigo.texto: Nio Taps EVE and Gotion for Trial Cell Batch as Firefly Owners Get a 17,000-Yuan Range Boost Published on 10/26/2026 at 14:21 | Editorial boerse-global.de Nio's in-house battery ambitions are edging toward the factory floor, but the company's more immediate commercial news is coming from its smallest model. Reports from battery-industry outlet Jipian Lab indicate that EVE Energy and Gotion High-Tech have been lined up to build a very small initial batch of Nio's own cylindrical cells, with volume production unlikely any time soon. The work remains in sampling, testing and pilot-manufacturing territory — a validation hurdle that makes a rapid jump to larger volumes difficult. That distinction matters. Nio develops the large-format cells internally and outsources the manufacturing, a route that differs from its earlier plan to build its own plant in Hefei, where equipment purchases were reportedly halted. The first cell version was unveiled in December 2023 with an energy density of 292 Wh/kg and 5C fast-charging capability — figures that describe the state of development at the time. The cell format has since moved beyond that original design, so the announced small series cannot simply be equated with the concept first presented. No Launch Date for the 120 kWh Pack The planned 120 kWh battery still has no start date. CEO William Li said on 7 August that development would continue, and the ET9 instead reached the market in December 2024 with a CATL battery. A successful first batch would therefore not signal an imminent launch for the planned pack, and no timetable for scaling production has been given. Li put spending on battery development at more than 2 billion yuan in September, underlining the project's weight for Nio without yet demonstrating a financial return. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Nio? CATL remains central in parallel. Nio is expanding its intake of prismatic CATL cells for Onvo and Firefly, so internal development and external supply run side by side — the expected trial production does not replace those relationships. Firefly Gains a Bigger Battery — at a Price On the product side, Firefly added a battery option on Friday that lifts its stated CLTC range from 420 to 560 kilometres. Existing owners can upgrade too, at a cost of 17,000 yuan. The offer is thus not confined to new buyers, though the range figure is a CLTC measure and should be read as such rather than as a promise for every driving situation. Firefly had already passed 90,000 cumulative deliveries on 16 October, giving the new option an established customer base to work with. How many owners will pay for the upgrade cannot be inferred from the launch alone. Deliveries provided the operating backdrop. Nio reported handover of the 160,000th third-generation ES8 in Xi'an on Friday — a model-specific milestone distinct from group-wide volume. On 17 October, president Qin Lihong cited Wilson data showing 111,638 retail sales across the three brands in China in the third quarter of 2026, ahead of BMW, Mercedes-Benz and Audi combined. That comparison is a China-market ranking, not a global one, and not a measure of the Nio brand alone. Concrete Steps Versus a Feasibility Study Beyond its current lineup, Nio is weighing further options. A Wednesday report said the company is examining the feasibility of vehicle assembly in Thailand, with no investment decision taken. The contrast in certainty is stark: the Firefly battery option and the delivery milestones are completed operational events, while Thai assembly remains under review. For investors, product offering and vehicle sales are the firmer anchors for now — and on the battery front, the naming of manufacturing partners makes the production path more concrete, even as the move to high-volume output and the launch of the planned vehicle pack stay unresolved. artigo.texto: Huawei's foray into the battery swapping industry has made NIO absolutely thrilled. NIO is no longer the "lone warrior in battery swapping" at last. On October 19, Zhiyue signed a strategic cooperation agreement on smart battery swapping ecosystem with CATL and E-Car Service, where the three parties will connect vehicles, battery swapping stations and the cloud, to promote the synergy between Huawei Qiankun and CATL's Choco-Swap network. Two points are particularly emphasized in the cooperation: First, to create a "smart and non-inductive energy replenishment" experience, where vehicles will realize a full-process intelligent closed loop of autonomously judging energy replenishment demands, searching for stations, entering stations, aligning positions, completing 99-second full-automatic battery swapping, and driving away independently. Second, Zhiyue will officially join CATL's Choco-Swap ecosystem, and work with strategic partners to jointly expand the battery swapping energy replenishment ecosystem around the adaptation and access of cooperative models to CATL's Choco-Swap network. In simple terms, the cooperation essentially leverages Huawei's intelligent driving capabilities, and with the help of CATL's battery swapping network, the intelligent driving system will independently decide "whether to swap the battery" and "where to swap the battery", so as to realize the smart and non-inductive energy replenishment experience. On the premise that the technology is fully verified, the relevant brands under Zhiyue including the Jing series will further launch battery swapping models. It is rumored that CATL and Zhiyue are advancing the development of the first batch of five battery swapping models, which are scheduled to be launched in 2027. Coincidentally, on October 22, BAIC Group also officially announced that it has signed a "million-unit" battery swapping strategic cooperation agreement with CATL. According to the agreement, BAIC Group will promote the access of adapted models of its multiple brands to CATL's Choco-Swap ecosystem, and strive for the target of one million battery swapping vehicles. It is worth noting that BAIC Group will also open its dealer network resources, while CATL's Choco-Swap will accelerate the station deployment relying on dealer stores, and the two sides will jointly explore the joint operation model. Although the battery swapping models of Huawei and BAIC, as well as their specific launch time, have not been officially confirmed, this series of "alliances and collaborations" has indeed brought a new trend: in the pure electric vehicle market, flash charging and ultra-fast charging are not the only solutions, and battery swapping is gaining recognition from more industrial players. What NIO has been waiting for is not just Huawei's entry When talking about battery swapping, NIO is an unavoidable name. Since its establishment more than ten years ago, NIO has always taken its battery swapping system capability as its "moat". However, battery swapping is a capital-intensive business, which requires investment in construction, maintenance and battery reserve. If it only relies on its own vehicle models, the scale and utilization rate of the battery swapping network will eventually be limited by sales volume. Therefore, from the very beginning, NIO has hoped that more players will join the big family of battery swapping. From another perspective, on the same track of battery swapping, NIO's experience in battery swapping can also be transformed into real competitive advantages. In fact, since November 2023, NIO has reached battery swapping cooperation with Changan Automobile, Geely Holding Group, Chery Automobile, JAC Group, Lotus, GAC Group, FAW Group and other enterprises. However, these "cooperation frameworks" are far less significant than the cooperation finalized between NIO and Geely. On September 28, NIO and Geely Holding reached a comprehensive strategic cooperation in the field of charging and battery swapping. According to the agreement, Geely will take a stake in NIO Energy with the equity of Yiyi Internet and cash, holding 30% of the shares after the transaction is completed; Geely will develop consumer-oriented battery swapping models, with NIO Energy providing battery swapping services. The fact that multiple battery swapping cooperations have been reached in the industry in a short period of time is by no means "child's play", but indicates that in the mainstream passenger vehicle market in the future, battery swapping models will no longer be exclusive to NIO. Geely, Huawei's Jing series brand will all launch competitive products in this field. From a competitive perspective, NIO has more rivals now, which may affect the sales of its own products. But for NIO, its first-mover advantage in battery swapping is still solid. What's more, the completion of a battery swapping station does not mean that the battery swapping business is successful. The bigger "hurdle" lies in operation. A battery swapping station needs a sufficient number of vehicles in continuous use to spread the costs of equipment, site, battery reserve and operation personnel. Car owners hope to have more stations nearby, while operators hope to get more orders from each station. The two sides restrict each other, which makes battery swapping easily fall into a vicious circle: the network is not large enough for users to choose battery swapping; without enough users, the network cannot continue to expand. This is also the reason why NIO keeps looking for partners. However, it must be made clear that as more participants join the battery swapping industry, whether the energy replenishment networks can be interconnected and whether the standards can be compatible is still a practical problem to be solved. artigo.texto: Supercharging is getting faster and faster. Why are car manufacturers setting their sights on battery swapping? In China's new energy vehicle industry, battery swapping has long been a niche route, but now this solution has suddenly become the focus of major industry players. On October 19, 2026, Huawei HiChord, CATL and E-Chen New Energy signed the "Strategic Cooperation Agreement for Intelligent Energy Replenishment Ecosystem". The three parties will strengthen cooperation in swappable batteries and battery swapping networks, and work with ecosystem partners to jointly build an intelligent battery swapping ecosystem. In the future, battery-swapping models equipped with Huawei's intelligent driving solution will support autonomous battery swapping. On October 22, BAIC and CATL signed a comprehensive agreement to deepen cooperation in battery swapping business. Multiple brand-adapted models under BAIC will be connected to CATL's Chocolate Battery Swapping Ecosystem. The two sides will jointly build a nationwide, highly interconnected public energy replenishment infrastructure network in the future. The question that follows is: with the advancement of ultra-fast charging technology and the gradual popularization of ultra-fast charging stations, the charging time of new energy vehicles has been continuously shortened, and the gap in energy replenishment time between charging and battery swapping is also narrowing. Why are so many automakers ramping up their investment in battery swapping? Ultra-fast Charging is Speeding Up, and Battery Swapping is Gaining Momentum Although at the early stage of the birth of new energy vehicles, automakers represented by BAIC and NIO began to deploy battery swapping technology, this solution has never become the mainstream energy replenishment method. The reason is that due to the separation of batteries and vehicles, compared with fast charging technology, the operation chain involved in battery swapping solutions is more complex. On the one hand, automakers cannot "work behind closed doors" and need to carry out overall design for models, batteries and battery swapping stations. As battery technology evolves rapidly, batteries of various models and specifications emerge in an endless stream, and battery swapping solutions will limit the technological iteration of automakers to a certain extent. Source: NIO On the other hand, in the context where cross-brand compatibility and network sharing are not yet sufficient, automakers need to bear large investment in station construction and operation, and large-scale promotion also faces considerable pressure. More importantly, as ultra-fast charging technology matures gradually, the comparative advantage of battery swapping solutions in "fast energy replenishment" will be weakened. Source: BYD For example, in March 2026, BYD launched the second-generation Blade Battery and its flash charging technology, which can achieve 10%-70% charge in 5 minutes, 10%-97% full charge in 9 minutes, and only takes 3 minutes longer than at room temperature at minus 30℃ for 20%-97% charging. The following month, CATL released its third-generation Shenxing ultra-fast charging battery, which delivers equivalent 10C and peak 15C ultra-fast charging capabilities, taking only 6 minutes and 27 seconds to charge from 10% to 98%. Source: Li Auto In April 2023, Ma Donghui, President and Chief Engineer of Li Auto, explained why Li Auto chose ultra-fast charging instead of battery swapping. Because electricity has no physical boundary, but battery swapping requires replacing the entire PACK (battery pack), which has physical boundaries. At the same time, achieving compatibility between different models and different brands is a huge challenge, which does not conform to Li Auto's principle of prioritizing efficiency. Different from the fact that it is difficult to form an effective unified standard for battery swapping, Ma Donghui believes that the charging gun standard is easier to unify and become a public resource, so he "does not think battery swapping can perform better than ultra-fast charging in the promotion of passenger vehicles." All in all, the thresholds such as technical adaptation, station investment and cross-brand collaboration have prevented battery swapping from becoming the mainstream energy replenishment method. The development of ultra-fast charging technology will further weaken the comparative advantage of battery swapping. With brands such as Feifan and Ruilan fading out, only NIO still adheres to the battery swapping technology route in the consumer market before. artigo.texto: Can CATL and automakers go back to the way they used to be? On October 21, 2026, CATL's A-share stock price dropped by 12%, marking the second-largest single-day decline since its listing. The Q3 financial report released the previous night showed that the revenue in the third quarter reached 1652 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 58.6%; the net profit attributable to shareholders was 212.5 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 14.5%, while the gross margin declined to some extent. The slowdown in profit growth stems from multiple factors: low-priced long-term energy storage orders signed in the past two years have entered the concentrated delivery period, and the proportion of energy storage sales has risen to about a quarter, leading to double dilution of the overall gross margin from low-margin businesses. In addition, the launch of consumption tax in September and the reduction of export tax rebates also increased the current-period costs. CATL also stated, "We are actively communicating with customers to share the relevant impacts together, and at the same time, we are promoting the implementation of new technologies and new products to reduce the impact on profitability." Negotiating with customers to share costs ostensibly aims to cope with short-term profit pressure, but behind it lies a longer-term issue in the power battery industry chain: how the value of the industry chain is distributed, and who holds the initiative. In the past, CATL occupied a pivotal position in the battery supply chain by virtue of its scale and technological advantages. However, this pattern is not static. In the past month, automakers have taken increasingly intensive actions around self-developed batteries, supplier selection and system integration. The so-called "de-CATL trend" is becoming a new force affecting the division of labor in the industry chain. This does not necessarily put automakers and CATL in opposition, but it may redefine the cooperation boundary between the two sides, and also becomes a key factor affecting CATL's future profit model. Automakers and CATL Start to Redraw Boundaries The "de-CATL trend" consists of a series of specific actions taken by different automakers. Li Auto has gone the farthest in this direction. At the earnings call in March this year, Li Auto stated that starting from 2026, all models of Li Auto will adopt a dual-battery route with both the "Li Auto brand" and the CATL brand. At the interim results call on August 26, Li Xiang said that starting from the second half of this year, Li Auto's self-developed batteries will be successively installed in all models. Later, Li Auto made a strategic capital increase of 2.65 billion yuan in Sunwoda Power. Combined with its previous shareholding, Li Auto holds 11.17% of the shares of Sunwoda Power, making it the second largest shareholder. At a communication meeting in September, representatives of Li Auto reiterated that starting from the new generation L8, all Li Auto models will be equipped with its self-developed batteries. The self-development model of Li Auto brand is that Li Auto takes the lead in cell design and R&D, while battery companies such as Sunwoda and CALB are responsible for cell production and manufacturing. At the battery pack level, BMS, thermal management and even insulating materials are independently developed, designed and produced by Li Auto. Judging from the current list of partners for Li Auto's self-developed batteries, CATL is no longer included. Reflected in the installation data, in June this year, Li Auto was still the fourth largest customer of CATL (accounting for 6.8%) and the fifth largest customer of Sunwoda (accounting for 6.4%). By August, Li Auto disappeared from the top five customers of CATL and became the largest customer of Sunwoda (accounting for 39%). XPeng Motors holds a similar attitude to Li Auto. In September 2026, He Xiaopeng publicly announced that "we will develop batteries independently starting from this year". Its route is similar: it takes the lead in defining the battery system, while cells continue to be purchased from external sources, and suppliers such as CALB and EVE Energy have been introduced. Xiaomi adopts a layered strategy. The newly launched range-extended products Pengcheng N70 and N90 will adopt the "Dragon Armor Battery", while according to previous reports, CATL remains the primary supplier for pure electric models under the main brand such as SU7 and YU7. For the "Dragon Armor Battery", cells are developed and manufactured by CALB and Sunwoda, but the product definition rights of battery pack structure, thermal management and BMS are in the hands of Xiaomi. AITO, which previously had close cooperation with CATL, also broke the pattern of "exclusive supply for all models" in 2026. The announcement from the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology shows that the pure electric version of AITO M6 has been equipped with an 81kWh LFP battery pack from Gotion High-Tech, and CALB has also entered AITO's supply system. Among traditional automakers, GAC's ENPOWER battery plant has been put into operation, realizing independent R&D and production; Geely integrated its battery assets to establish Jiyao Pass in 2025, and continues to promote independent R&D. Looking back at these actions of automakers, their purpose is not necessarily to kick CATL out of the game. More of them want to reduce their dependence on a single supplier, which does not mean that CATL has lost its product competitiveness. The most important means is to separate "cell procurement" from "battery pack manufacturing". Through this separation, automakers have redrawn the boundary of the supply chain, clarifying which manufacturing links can be outsourced and which definition rights and integration rights must be kept in their own hands, thus changing the power relationship between automakers and battery manufacturers. artigo.texto: The follow-on deal, signed through its U.S. subsidiary Samsung SDI America, lifts the total volume contracted with AOP to 1.5 GWh after an initial order late last year. AOP will deploy the systems, due for delivery by year-end, at a large-scale Texas power project set to break ground next year. The order covers the Samsung Battery Box 1.7, an all-in-one unit built with high-nickel NCA cells at StarPlus Energy, Samsung SDI's Indiana joint venture with Stellantis. It packs 17 percent more energy density than its predecessor into the same 20-foot container and holds NFPA 855 and UL 9540 safety certifications. All three Korean battery makers are retooling U.S. electric vehicle lines for energy storage as EV demand cools, and Samsung SDI's turn has gathered pace this year. It landed a 1.5 trillion won ($1.13 billion) U.S. ESS order in March and agreed in August to buy General Motors' stake in their Indiana joint venture, with storage batteries the near-term priority. Samsung SDI says it is the only non-Chinese maker of prismatic ESS batteries in North America, a format it says outlasts pouch cells in durability and fire safety. The company is in talks with several other U.S. customers and expects further orders soon. "Alpha Omega Power is one of the fastest growing independent power producers in the country, and the kind of sophisticated operator we want to partner with to tackle grid reliability challenges," said Fabrice Hudry, executive vice president and head of the ESS team at Samsung SDI America. He said the company would widen its footing in North America through "differentiated technology and local production capabilities." AJP Takeaways - Samsung SDI said on Oct. 26, 2026 that its U.S. unit had signed a 1 GWh energy storage supply deal with Alpha Omega Power, bringing their total contracts to 1.5 GWh. - The SBB 1.7 units will be made at StarPlus Energy in Indiana, Samsung SDI's joint venture with Stellantis, for a Texas power project due to break ground in 2027. - The order follows Samsung SDI's 1.5 trillion won U.S. ESS deal in March 2026 and its August 2026 agreement to buy General Motors' stake in their Indiana battery joint venture. artigo.texto: Samsung SDI has secured a 1-gigawatt-hour energy storage system supply deal with US power developer Alpha Omega Power, bringing their combined contracts to 1.5 GWh as the Korean battery maker expands its North American business. The latest agreement, signed through Samsung SDI's Michigan-based subsidiary, follows an initial deal made last year, the company said Monday. The StarPlus Energy plant in Kokomo, Indiana, will produce the battery cells and modules, with deliveries scheduled by year-end. Samsung SDI will supply its Samsung Battery Box 1.7, an integrated ESS solution using high-nickel nickel-cobalt-aluminum prismatic batteries. The system offers 17 percent higher energy density than its predecessor, SBB 1.5, within the same 20-foot container. It also features AI-based monitoring to detect abnormalities and predict battery life. For fire protection, SBB 1.7 uses Samsung SDI's Enhanced Direct Injection technology, which delivers fire-extinguishing agents directly into battery modules. The company said the system complies with US fire safety standard NFPA 855 and holds UL 9540 certification. AOP plans to deploy the batteries at large-scale power projects in the western US and Texas, where construction is expected to begin next year. The projects aim to support grid reliability as electricity demand rises. "American-made ESS from Samsung SDI will play an important role in AOP's continued growth," said Alpha Omega Power CEO Paul Choi. "This second agreement strengthens our domestic supply chain supporting the next generation of energy infrastructure." Samsung SDI is seeking additional ESS contracts in North America, positioning its locally manufactured prismatic batteries as an alternative to Chinese suppliers. Fabrice Hudry, head of Samsung SDI America's ESS team, said the company plans to expand its regional business by leveraging its battery technology and US production capabilities. yejinlim@heraldcorp.com

artigo.texto: Key Takeaways - HiTHIUM, a stationary energy storage manufacturer with more than 200 GWh of cumulative deliveries, has formally entered the Canadian market with Toronto as its main hub. - The company is offering a 4-hour system built on its 6.25 MWh “∞Power” container and a 6.9 MWh 8-hour lithium-ion system that it describes as the first native 8-hour lithium-ion product. - A new 4 MWh sodium-ion system supporting 2 to 8 hours of storage is aimed at very cold regions such as Northern Canada. - HiTHIUM has offices in British Columbia and Alberta, plus sites in Quebec, Yellowknife and Fort Smith. - A UL Solutions fire test at the start of 2026 left the burning 6.25 MWh container structurally intact, with no thermal propagation to units placed 15 cm away. HiTHIUM has announced its entry into Canada, bringing 4-hour and 8-hour battery energy storage systems (BESS) and a sodium-ion product built for extreme cold to a market that is adding grid-scale storage quickly. The Toronto-based launch was announced on Oct. 21, 2026. HiTHIUM Sets Up Canadian Operations The manufacturer works only on stationary energy storage and says it ranks among the top two suppliers worldwide for storage components, with cumulative delivered capacity now above 200 GWh. Toronto will serve as the center of its Canadian business. HiTHIUM also runs subsidiary offices in British Columbia and Alberta, along with operating sites in Quebec and in the northern communities of Yellowknife and Fort Smith. Storage Demand in Canada According to the company, Canada’s installed storage base is expected to double between 2025 and 2027, while combined wind, solar and storage capacity in the country is projected to hit 50 GW by 2035. The company is pitching its utility-scale products into that buildout, which is part of the wider growth covered on the iGrowNews battery storage news page. Alongside its lithium-ion lineup, the company introduced a 4 MWh sodium-ion system. HiTHIUM says the product is built for a very long service life, can be configured for 2 to 8 hours of storage, and suits harsh, cold climates like those in Canada’s north. HiTHIUM Executives on the Canadian Push “We are committed to delivering Canadian customers advanced, robust solutions, from 8-hour long duration energy storage to extreme-weather-ready sodium-ion BESS. But this also means being present for customers wherever they are, able to serve them quickly and locally. While Toronto serves as the main hub for our Canadian operations, we have subsidiary offices in British Columbia and Alberta, as well as operating sites in Quebec, Yellowknife, and Fort Smith,” said Mizhi Zhang, President of Global Business at HiTHIUM. “Canada’s ambitious clean energy targets, as well as its high safety and regulatory standards, require partners who can deliver advanced technology that’s also tested and compliance-ready. At the same time, project developers have to consider the tough climate. As a vertically integrated, global solutions provider, HiTHIUM is structured to meet exactly this nexus of challenges. Our strategy of advancing both lithium-ion and sodium-ion storage is designed to offer customers in markets like Canada the benefits of flexibility, since we see these technologies as highly complementary,” Zhang added. “Our partners, whether major energy developers, public utilities, or industrial enterprises, rely on our readiness for local certification and our long-term bankability to support them, from permitting through project commissioning,” said Jordan Hebbert, Senior Manager of Canada at HiTHIUM. “Likewise, they depend on the proven durability of HiTHIUM technology—including performance even in extreme weather conditions. In fact, long-term operational data from North American and European projects has recently demonstrated systems outperforming even our guarantees. And we offer customers a wider range of durations and choice of chemistries because we understand that they’re coming to us with a very diverse range of energy storage needs,” Hebbert said. Matching Duration to Project Needs The 4-hour offering is based on the “∞Power” 6.25 MWh container, which uses a 1175 Ah cell made by HiTHIUM. The company says most projects now planned in Canada are sized around this 4-hour unit, which lets operators move wind, solar and baseload generation into later peak periods, support grid reliability and absorb more renewable output as electrification pushes demand up. The design packs more capacity into a standard 20-foot container, and units can be installed back-to-back and side-to-side to shrink a site’s footprint. HiTHIUM’s 8-Hour Lithium-Ion System For longer discharge, HiTHIUM offers a 6.9 MWh 8-hour BESS using its own 1300 Ah cells. The company says the system uses fewer parts, carries a 25-year lifespan and is intended to reduce renewable curtailment and serve industries that cannot tolerate downtime, such as AI data centers. HiTHIUM argues that wind developers and data center operators can both gain lower risk and steadier revenue from 8-hour storage, a theme that runs through much of the renewable energy sector. Fire Test Results Early in 2026, HiTHIUM and UL Solutions carried out an independent fire test on the safety design of the 6.25 MWh block. One container burned under extreme conditions for 24 hours with its doors open to maximize heat spread, while neighboring containers sat only 15 cm away and only passive safety systems were active. After the test, the burned container remained structurally intact, fire did not spread between containers, and cell temperatures in the adjacent units stayed below safety limits, according to the company.

artigo.texto: Beno T&R Wins First Order Since Launching Semiconductor Division; US Battery Project Worth KRW 5.2 Billion KOSDAQ-listed Beno T&R has secured its first order since establishing its Semiconductor Division, expanding its business into semiconductor and battery engineering. Beno T&R disclosed on October 26 that it had signed a KRW 5.2 billion contract to participate in a project to build a U.S. production facility for a global North American battery manufacturer. The contract value is equivalent to approximately 110% of the company’s revenue in its most recent fiscal year, and the contract period runs from October 1, 2026, to July 31, 2027. As part of the project, Beno T&R will install secondary battery control controllers at a battery manufacturing facility in the United States and carry out related utility hook-up work. The company said the order is significant because it marks the first achievement of its recently established Semiconductor Division. Beno T&R has maintained its existing construction business while developing its bio and robotics businesses as future growth drivers. However, it decided to expand into semiconductor and battery equipment after determining that those businesses would need more time to generate substantial revenue. The project will apply the company’s technology for supplying high-purity chemicals used in semiconductor processes to battery manufacturing processes. The company also expects that participating in a global battery manufacturer’s U.S. facility construction project will give it a track record that could help it enter the North American secondary battery supply chain. Beno T&R plans to first complete the project reliably and on schedule to establish a record of supplying the North American market. The company said that, because the equipment will operate in connection with the battery production line, demand could arise for additional related equipment and auxiliary facilities as the production line is expanded or processes are upgraded. Building on this supply agreement, the company aims to continue discussions on supplying follow-on equipment for the project and generate additional revenue for its Semiconductor Division. At the same time, it plans to use this track record to diversify its customer base for chemical supply systems used in semiconductor and battery manufacturing processes. “This order marks the first achievement since the establishment of our Semiconductor Division and is also significant because it represents our first participation in a North American battery project,” said Shin Dongbeom, CEO of Beno T&R. “We will supply the equipment for the contracted project reliably and on schedule, build our customer’s trust, and turn this into follow-on equipment orders as we develop semiconductor and battery engineering into core businesses for the company.” He added, “We will also continue to develop our bio and robotics businesses as medium- to long-term growth drivers and maintain a balanced business portfolio.” Hot Picks Today "Koreans Spend 1 Million Won Each and Come Back"... Domestic battery makers are also increasing ESS production to meet rising demand. "LG Energy Solution plans to secure annual production capacity of more than 50 GWh for LFP batteries for ESS in North America by the end of 2026. Samsung SDI and SK On are also working to expand ESS supply through U.S. production and the conversion of existing facilities," Han said. "As customers increase their production, supply volumes of modules, thermal management components, and cooling systems used in batteries could also rise." Han named Sebang Battery, Shinsung ST, and Hanjung NCS as companies to watch, saying that increased ESS production by domestic battery makers and the expansion of local production in North America could lead to more orders for modules, components, and cooling systems. Please enter the email address you use for your account so we can send you a link to reset your password: Most Americans still say they would oppose a data center being built near where they live, but the facilities’ standing has improved among Republicans, a new Heatmap Pro poll finds. The American public’s backlash against data centers may finally be starting to slow down, although the facilities remain staggeringly unpopular, a new poll finds. Seventy-one percent of Americans said they would oppose a data center being built near where they live, according to a new Heatmap Pro poll conducted by Embold Research earlier this month. That is an abysmal finding for technology companies and would-be developers of the computing facilities. But it actually represents an improvement from previous polling, and it suggests one of the fastest shifts in public opinion in recent memory may be tapering off. That shift has been swift. As recently as September of last year, about 43% of Americans said they would support a data center being built near where they live, and Americans broadly appeared to be evenly split on the infrastructure, according to Heatmap Pro polling. Eleven months later, 75% of Americans told the same poll that they would oppose a nearby data center — a 32 point shift. That monumental turnaround helped make data centers a defining issue in this election cycle. That backlash has transformed the economics of the data center boom, the largest infrastructure buildout in recent U.S. history. The overwhelming majority of data center projects now face some degree of community opposition, Heatmap Pro reporting suggests. More than $260 billion in proposed data centers have been canceled this year after meeting local opposition. The artificial intelligence company Anthropic even flagged the infrastructure slowdown on Monday when it filed for its initial public offering, which is widely expected to be among the largest ever. Now our new survey shows that Americans’ rejection of the enormous computing facilities may itself be slowing. The small observed drop, which only slightly exceeds the survey’s margin of error, was driven by a four-point decline in the share of Americans who said they would “strongly oppose” the technology. While Americans of all parties improved their view of data centers, the change was most pronounced among Republicans. In August, 23% of GOP voters said that they would support a data center being built near where they live. In the new poll, conducted after weeks of favorable campaigning by President Trump, 34% of Republicans said they would support a data center slated for their area, while the share of Republicans who said they would oppose it fell from 66% to 58%. Data centers’ standing among independents improved by nine points during the same period. Democrats remain largely unified against the infrastructure, and data centers’ improvement among that group was just outside the margin of error. While Americans of every age, race, gender, and partisan ID remain more opposed to local data center development than in favor of it, their standing has also improved among men since the summer. In August, 21% of men said they would support a data center being built near where they live. Now, 28% of men would support one.

artigo.texto: Promover a produção com baixas emissões. Desde a transformação das técnicas agrícolas e a utilização de subprodutos agrícolas até a construção de marcas de produtos agrícolas de baixa emissão, as principais áreas agrícolas da província mantêm e desenvolvem práticas de agricultura circular, adaptando-se às mudanças climáticas, abrindo oportunidades para agregar valor aos produtos agrícolas, aumentar a competitividade e participar gradualmente do mercado de créditos de carbono. Na área de agricultura orgânica do bairro de Lang Biang, em Da Lat , a fazenda do Sr. Nguyen Thanh Hai reestruturou suas plantações, praticando a rotação de dezenas de tipos de frutas e verduras que, ao longo dos anos, têm sido consumidas pelo mercado, com aumento da produção e agregação de valor. Assim, em seus mais de 1,5 hectares de terra com certificação orgânica, o Sr. Hai organiza o plantio de diferentes hortaliças em áreas separadas, seguindo um cronograma de plantio contínuo. Ao final de cada ciclo de produção, ele trata o solo e passa a plantar tomates, acelga chinesa, espinafre, alface e dente-de-leão, antes de retornar ao plantio de pimentões. O espinafre tem um ciclo de cultivo de cerca de 35 a 40 dias; amaranto, couve-flor, aipo e brócolis são cultivados em rotação, de acordo com suas características de crescimento e as condições climáticas em diferentes épocas. Para obter a certificação orgânica no início de 2023, o Sr. Hai investiu amplamente em infraestrutura, melhoria do solo e ajustes nos processos agrícolas, incluindo um sistema de irrigação automatizado, áreas para mistura de esterco com subprodutos da colheita e a produção de pesticidas biológicos para o controle de pragas. “Os primeiros ciclos de cultivo enfrentaram dificuldades devido a problemas de saúde do solo após o uso prolongado de fertilizantes e pesticidas inorgânicos. Portanto, a transição geral para a agricultura de baixa emissão exige que os produtores equilibrem os nutrientes orgânicos, controlem pragas e doenças usando soluções biológicas integradas e mantenham um ecossistema agrícola estável, adequado às condições e características do solo”, compartilhou o Sr. Hai. Na comuna de Quang Lap, a fazenda orgânica Thien Sinh vem aprimorando e expandindo continuamente sua área de cultivo orgânico e criação de animais há quase 20 anos, atingindo 15 hectares. Isso inclui 10 hectares dedicados à rotação de culturas de hortaliças e frutas, produzindo de 1,5 a 2 toneladas de produtos por dia. Os 5 hectares restantes são destinados a forragem, currais, pastagens naturais para gado e porcos criados soltos, oficinas e armazenamento refrigerado para o processamento e conservação pós-colheita de hortaliças. Comparadas às hortaliças cultivadas convencionalmente, as hortaliças cultivadas organicamente rendem cerca de 70% mais, sendo vendidas a preços 2,5 a 3 vezes maiores. Além disso, a fazenda desenvolveu um rebanho de mais de 50 bovinos de alta produção e centenas de porcos híbridos, alimentados com ração processada localmente. Simultaneamente, utiliza materiais biológicos para cama dos animais, compostando-os com subprodutos agrícolas para criar fertilizante orgânico que fornece nutrientes para as hortaliças e frutas. O proprietário da fazenda, Nguyen Quoc Thang, disse: “A fazenda é inspecionada e avaliada regularmente por órgãos competentes para garantir a qualidade dos padrões orgânicos para vegetais, frutas e todo o processo de criação de animais. Como resultado, a fazenda recebeu a certificação orgânica pela terceira vez, válida até 2028. O mercado interno reconheceu os benefícios dos produtos agrícolas orgânicos e os consome muito rapidamente. O mercado internacional está fazendo grandes encomendas, então precisamos continuar investindo e expandindo a escala da agricultura e criação de animais com baixa emissão de carbono no futuro…” Promovendo o selo "Baixa Emissão" Estatísticas mostram que a província possui atualmente cerca de 110.700 hectares de produção agrícola de alta tecnologia. Desse total, cerca de 2.100 hectares são destinados à agricultura orgânica, com a meta de expansão para 11.200 hectares até 2030. Para 2050, a província almeja que 100% de suas principais culturas adotem técnicas de cultivo sustentáveis; estabelecer um banco de dados digitalizado conectado ao sistema nacional de monitoramento; e construir e popularizar gradualmente o selo de "Baixa Emissão" para produtos agrícolas, melhorando a eficiência no uso de recursos e a qualidade de vida da população. De acordo com o plano de ação do Comitê Popular Provincial até 2035, toda a província pretende reduzir as emissões totais de gases de efeito estufa da produção agrícola em pelo menos 15% em comparação com 2020; a taxa de resíduos agrícolas coletados e reutilizados na economia circular deverá atingir mais de 80%. A área de terras cultivadas aplicando padrões de produção sustentável e reduzindo as emissões deverá atingir mais de 30% da área total cultivada da província. Além disso, a província selecionará diversos modelos agrícolas com potencial para gerar créditos de carbono, atendendo aos requisitos de organizações internacionais. Para alcançar esses objetivos, o Comitê Popular Provincial orientou os departamentos e agências competentes a revisar a estrutura de produção e identificar áreas adequadas para a implementação de soluções de agricultura sustentável. Áreas de produção ineficientes estão sendo destinadas à conversão para o cultivo de culturas de alto valor econômico e baixa emissão, com potencial para geração de créditos de carbono, adequadas às condições ecológicas e às demandas do mercado.

artigo.texto: Time- and Cost-Burdening SW Code Verification… 'AI Supervision Team' Emerges to Solve Inefficiency Kim Ki-seop, Professor in the Department of Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Information Technology at Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology (DGIST) Development of LLM-Based Software Development, Analysis, and Security Automation Technologies "Multiple AI Agents Simultaneously Review Code… Saving Time and Costs" Verification of software (SW) code generated by artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a new challenge. Whether written by humans or AI, deploying code to actual services without review can lead to errors and security incidents. The procedure to prevent this is 'code review,' which involves examining the functionality, quality, and security issues of the code. Because such code reviews also require significant time and cost, research into automating them with AI has continued. Most approaches have centered on a single AI reviewing the entire codebase. Kim Ki-seop, Professor in the Department of Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Information Technology at Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology (DGIST), said, "It is like having a single building inspector check everything from design to finishing alone," adding that it is "inefficient in terms of time, cost, and other aspects." Professor Kim's research team created an 'AI Supervision Team' where multiple AIs with divided roles review code together. One AI verifies whether the code has been implemented according to the design, while another identifies security vulnerabilities. Yet another checks whether the team's established coding rules have been followed. However, as the number of AIs and items to review increases, errors may occur where the code review deviates from its original purpose. The AI agents continue conversations with each other, effectively forgetting the initial supervision objective. To prevent this, the research team added an AI called a 'QA (Quality Assurance) Checker' that oversees the entire supervision team. Its role is to correct course when there is a risk of the AI agents losing the direction of the code review. Professor Kim stated, "The core function of the QA Checker is to ensure that the AI code review team properly reaches its initial goal." Professor Kim's research team will directly introduce this technology at the '2026 K-Premier Deep Tech Festa' (Registration: https://vvd.bz/buvX), held on the 29th at COEX in Seoul. Professor Kim is also conducting research into examining the thinking processes of AI models. Just as stimulating specific areas of the human brain activates language or physical functions, this research aims to identify neurons within AI that handle specific functions. Professor Kim said, "I was curious whether there are separate neurons responsible for each language inside an AI, and if removing those parts would truly disable that language capability." Analysis results showed that removing neurons responsible for a specific language actually reduced the ability in that language. However, there were also cases where abilities in other languages declined simultaneously. Professor Kim explained, "If we only remove the neurons responsible for Japanese but Korean becomes clumsy as well, we must preserve the neurons among them that affect Korean," adding, "This way, we can accurately remove only the target to be deleted while using the remaining knowledge as before." The research team is also conducting studies on enhancing specific neurons to boost corresponding capabilities. This research connects to technology for erasing knowledge that AI has already learned. In December 2024, the Indian Publishers Association, with participation from Bloomsbury, the publisher of Harry Potter, filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, claiming that ChatGPT provided book summaries without permission. The publishers demanded that if license agreements would not be signed, the training data should be deleted. However, retraining an AI from scratch to erase already learned content costs tens of billions of won. Professor Kim is researching methods to store knowledge in easily erasable locations from the learning stage. Citing a classroom environment composed of multiple separate blackboards as an example, he said, "If we need to erase Harry Potter content, it would be like removing only the Harry Potter auxiliary blackboard," adding, "AI can be designed from the start to facilitate 'partial deletion.'" Professor Kim emphasized, "The technologies I am researching will fundamentally align with the concerns of most AI companies," stating, "I want to better understand the needs of domestic companies and provide directly applicable technologies, thereby contributing to our country's economic development." artigo.texto: CCC chairs carbon markets panel The CCC’s chairmanship of the IACCM builds on its existing leadership functions in national climate policy and reporting. The Climate Change Commission (CCC) welcomes its designation as chair of the Inter-Agency Committee on Carbon Markets (IACCM) under Executive Order (EO) 127, which establishes a governance framework for the Philippines’ participation in international carbon markets under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement and in the Voluntary Carbon Market. Signed by President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., EO 127 institutionalizes the country’s climate change mitigation efforts and seeks to unlock international climate finance. As IACCM chair, the CCC will guide inter-agency coordination and help ensure that carbon market policies support the Philippines’ Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), national greenhouse gas inventory, and climate transparency reporting obligations under the Paris Agreement. The Commission will also serve as the committee’s Secretariat and provide technical and administrative support. This move supports the direction set by the Philippine Development Plan 20230-2028, particularly Chapter 15 on accelerating climate action and strengthening disaster resilience. The chapter calls for stronger collaboration with the private sector and the international community to scale up sustainable and green investments. It also advances the transition to a low-carbon economy while promoting economic growth and resilience. “Carbon markets can help advance these goals by providing an additional channel for private capital and international climate finance. Credible carbon projects can support emissions reduction and other climate solutions. Clear rules and reliable accounting will help protect environmental integrity and give investors greater certainty,” said CCC vice chairperson and executive director Robert E.A. Borje. The CCC’s chairmanship builds on its existing leadership functions in national climate policy and reporting. As Secretariat of the NDC Technical Working Group, the Commission supports the assessment of sectoral policies and measures against the country’s NDC. It also supports the monitoring, reporting, and verification of NDC implementation and the fulfillment of national and international reporting requirements. Under Executive Order 174, s. 2014, the CCC serves as the overall lead agency for the Philippine National Greenhouse Gas Inventory. It coordinates and consolidates emissions data from sector lead agencies. This information provides an important evidence base for national climate policy and emissions accounting.

artigo.texto: In the U.S. energy storage system (ESS) market, traditionally dominated by lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) batteries, Samsung SDI has successfully secured a large-scale supply contract utilizing ternary batteries. Samsung SDI announced on October 26 that its Americas subsidiary (SDIA) has signed an ESS solution supply contract with the U.S. energy firm Alpha Omega Power (AOP) for a capacity of 1 gigawatt-hour (GWh). Combined with a previous phase-one contract late last year, the total volume reaches 1.5 GWh. The supply will be delivered within the year, and AOP plans to deploy it in a large-scale power project breaking ground in Texas next year. While the contract amount is private, industry observers estimate the price of ESS solutions at roughly $160 to $200 per kilowatt-hour (kWh). For 1 GWh, this translates to $160 million to $200 million, or approximately 210 billion to 260 billion Korean won. Batteries are classified into types like prismatic and pouch depending on how the cell is encased. The batteries supplied by Samsung SDI this time are prismatic batteries. Prismatic cells are enclosed in a hard metal can, offering greater impact resistance and higher fire safety compared to pouch types housed in thin film pouches. Among non-Chinese battery manufacturers with North American production facilities, Samsung SDI is the only one producing prismatic batteries for ESS applications. The product being supplied is not just a standalone cell, but a solution called ‘SBB (Samsung Battery Box) 1.7’. It packs not only prismatic battery cells but also cooling and fire-suppression systems, along with battery management software, into a container approximately 6 meters long. Unlike the method of delivering only battery cells, this integrated approach minimizes the need for clients to assemble multiple devices separately, making installation much simpler. The battery chemistry relies on nickel-cobalt-aluminum (NCA) ternary cells. ESS applications with fewer spatial constraints typically utilize LFP batteries, which are cheaper and have longer lifespans. However, although ternary batteries are more expensive, they pack more electricity into the same space and deliver instant high power. Power grids must maintain a stable frequency (60Hz) by balancing supply and demand; when imbalances occur due to power plant failures, ESS systems instantly discharge or absorb electricity to correct it. Company officials explain that ternary batteries are advantageous for projects requiring massive power output in short bursts. Production will be handled by StarPlus Energy (SPE), an Indiana-based joint venture factory between Samsung SDI and Stellantis. Although originally an electric vehicle battery plant, some lines have been repurposed for ESS production since October of last year to navigate a temporary slowdown in U.S. EV demand. Fabrice Hudry, head of the SDIA ESS team and vice president, stated, “We will continue to expand our business foundation in the North American ESS market through differentiated technological competitiveness and local production.”

artigo.texto: Itaipu financia data centers de IA, mas no Paraguai Paraguai atrai megaprojeto americano de infraestrutura para inteligência artificial usando energia de Itaipu. O Brasil bancou US$ 89,8 bilhões da usina e pode ficar para trás na corrida. O vice-secretário de Estado dos EUA, Christopher Landau, visitou a usina de Itaipu nesta semana e anunciou uma parceria estratégica entre a americana Crusoe e a paraguaia Araico para construir um megaprojeto de infraestrutura voltado à inteligência artificial. A eletricidade que vai alimentar os servidores é a mesma de Itaipu, empreendimento quase inteiramente financiado por empréstimos garantidos pelo Tesouro Nacional brasileiro. A ironia é difícil de ignorar. O Brasil pagou US$ 89,8 bilhões em custos líquidos desde o início das operações da usina, segundo dados do Instituto Acende Brasil. O Paraguai obteve receitas de US$ 5,9 bilhões no mesmo período. E agora é o país vizinho que sai na frente para capturar o maior ciclo de investimentos em infraestrutura tecnológica da década. O projeto de IA que pode mudar o Paraguai O Departamento de Estado americano classificou a parceria Crusoe-Araico como “potencialmente um dos maiores investimentos privados na história do Paraguai”. A primeira fase do projeto deve entrar em operação em meados de 2027, oferecendo serviços de cloud computing para consumidores nos Estados Unidos e na América Latina. A Araico planeja construir o Iguazi AI City, um campus de data centers com meta de atingir até 1,3 GW de capacidade total no longo prazo. Para se ter ideia da escala, isso equivale a mais da metade da capacidade contratada de toda a usina de Itaipu pelo lado paraguaio. Além do acordo de IA, a Uranium Energy Corp anunciou um investimento de US$ 12 milhões para desenvolver concessões de exploração de urânio em solo paraguaio. A visita de Landau foi acompanhada por uma delegação comercial focada em tecnologia, minerais críticos, infraestrutura fluvial e logística. O presidente paraguaio Santiago Peña acompanhou pessoalmente o tour pela hidrelétrica. Por que o Paraguai tem vantagem sobre o Brasil A equação é simples: energia barata, abundante e disponível. O Paraguai tem direito a 50% da geração de Itaipu e 50% da geração de Yaciretá, usina em sociedade com a Argentina. Mas o consumo interno paraguaio é uma fração dessa capacidade. Em 2025, o país usou apenas 36% da sua fatia de Itaipu. Marcos Peigo, CEO da Scala Data Centers, uma das maiores empresas do setor na América Latina, afirmou que o Paraguai tem potencial para atingir 1 GW em data centers antes do Brasil, caso o país não aprove rapidamente incentivos tributários estaduais para a indústria. O governo paraguaio, segundo Peigo, “fez a lição de casa de rodar o mundo com o presidente” e está cumprindo suas promessas ao mercado. O Brasil aprovou recentemente o Redata no Congresso, programa de incentivos fiscais para data centers. Mas a implementação depende de adesão dos estados, e o ritmo da burocracia brasileira pode custar posições numa corrida global que se mede em meses, não em anos. A conta desproporcional de Itaipu para o brasileiro O tratado binacional de Itaipu, assinado em 1973, foi desenhado para permitir que o Paraguai, com economia muito menor, conseguisse arcar com seus compromissos. Claudio Sales, presidente do Acende Brasil, reconhece que “o desenho do tratado é de uma brilhante engenharia diplomática”, mas afirma que negociações desfavoráveis ao Brasil nas últimas duas décadas distorceram os números além do razoável. Em 2009, um acordo entre os presidentes Lula e Fernando Lugo aumentou os pagamentos brasileiros pela fatia de energia não utilizada pelos paraguaios. Hoje, o Paraguai recebe 59% dos repasses financeiros da usina, enquanto 89% dos custos ficam com o lado brasileiro. As despesas socioambientais da usina ilustram o problema. Até 2016, essas despesas ficavam em torno de US$ 100 milhões por ano. Em 2022, saltaram para US$ 505 milhões. Em 2025, atingiram US$ 1,2 bilhão. Parte desses recursos foi direcionada para fins desconectados da operação da usina, como obras para a COP-30 no Pará e apoio à Universidade Federal de Integração Latino-Americana. “Essas despesas viraram um verdadeiro orçamento paralelo que, por Itaipu ser fruto de um tratado binacional, não se sujeita aos controles do Tribunal de Contas da União e do Congresso”, afirmou Sales. Tudo isso é repassado à tarifa de energia e bancado pelo consumidor brasileiro na conta de luz. O que está em jogo para o Brasil na corrida dos data centers A demanda global por infraestrutura de IA está redefinindo a geopolítica energética. Países com energia barata e regulação ágil estão atraindo bilhões em investimentos. A corrida por data centers se tornou um dos vetores mais relevantes de desenvolvimento econômico no mundo. O Brasil tem a maior matriz elétrica renovável entre as grandes economias, com capacidade instalada superior a 200 GW. Mas enfrenta gargalos regulatórios, tributários e de transmissão que dificultam a conversão dessa vantagem em projetos concretos. Enquanto isso, o Paraguai oferece ao mercado americano exatamente o que ele procura: energia limpa, preço competitivo e velocidade de implementação. A situação cria um paradoxo incômodo. O contribuinte brasileiro financiou a construção e a operação de Itaipu por décadas. O custo aparece na conta de luz de cada residência e empresa do país. E agora, a energia excedente dessa mesma usina pode se tornar a base da infraestrutura de inteligência artificial da América Latina, gerando empregos, receita fiscal e posicionamento estratégico para o Paraguai. Para o investidor brasileiro, o recado é claro: a vantagem energética do país não se traduz automaticamente em vantagem competitiva. Sem agilidade regulatória e incentivos claros, o Brasil corre o risco de assistir seus vizinhos colherem os frutos de uma infraestrutura que ele mesmo ajudou a construir. artigo.texto: Elea prevê impactos do Redata só em 2027 Companhia espera efeitos após regulamentação e detalha projetos no Rio de Janeiro e em Belém para atender demandas de nuvem e IA. A Elea Data Centers prevê que os impactos do Redata sobre seus negócios começarão a aparecer em 2027, após a regulamentação e a definição dos equipamentos contemplados pelos incentivos. Em entrevista à TV Síntese, Fernanda Belchior, diretora de marketing e vendas da companhia, apresentou essa expectativa e detalhou os planos de expansão no Rio de Janeiro e em Belém, voltados ao atendimento de cargas de computação em nuvem e inteligência artificial. A definição das Nomenclaturas Comuns do Mercosul (NCMs) dos equipamentos e dos procedimentos de aplicação do regime precisam ser equacionadas para que os efeitos se concretizem. Belchior avalia que o Redata amplia as condições para aquisição de equipamentos importados sem equivalentes nacionais e sinaliza segurança jurídica aos investidores. A diretora ressalta, porém, que o crescimento do setor não depende exclusivamente dos incentivos. De acordo com ela, o mercado de data centers já avança a taxas de dois dígitos, impulsionado pela nuvem, enquanto a inteligência artificial deve ampliar a demanda por infraestrutura. Os efeitos do regime, em sua avaliação, serão percebidos principalmente a médio e longo prazo, acompanhando o desenvolvimento dos empreendimentos. “Mas a gente precisa agir agora, para que a gente consiga colher esses resultados nesse futuro próximo”, afirmou. Belém terá implantação por etapas Na capital paraense, a Elea planeja um data center com capacidade de carga de TI que pode chegar a 5 MW, começando com 1 MW. A implantação será faseada conforme as necessidades do cliente âncora. Segundo Belchior, há uma negociação em andamento, cujos detalhes permanecem confidenciais. A executiva informou que o projeto dispõe de uma garantia inicial de 7,5 MW de energia e terá uma subestação próxima ao terreno. Esse volume de fornecimento energético é distinto da capacidade destinada às cargas de TI. O empreendimento deverá atender aplicações de inteligência artificial e de computação em nuvem. A companhia também mantém conversas com federações, associações, operadoras e provedores locais para identificar demandas e preparar a conectividade da instalação. “A gente entende que Belém é uma rota complementar à Fortaleza, que já é um hub super estabelecido no Nordeste”, disse Belchior. Segundo a diretora, o sistema de refrigeração previsto para a unidade não utilizará água. A infraestrutura de telecomunicações está sendo discutida paralelamente ao desenvolvimento do projeto, incluindo topologias de rede e necessidades dos potenciais clientes. Rio AI City tem 250 MW de energia garantida No Rio de Janeiro, Belchior afirmou que a Elea já tem 250 MW de energia garantida para a etapa inicial de expansão do Rio AI City. O projeto prevê um horizonte de 1,5 GW em um cenário de 2030 em diante, com autorizações e implantação por fases. A empresa já opera o RJ01, com capacidade informada de 4 MW, voltado a cargas de nuvem. A expansão ocorrerá com a construção modular de outras unidades para aplicações de cloud e inteligência artificial, acompanhando a demanda dos clientes âncora. Mesmo com os 250 MW de energia assegurados, a operação começará com capacidade inferior a esse volume, explicou a executiva. O avanço também dependerá da preparação da infraestrutura de transmissão, das subestações e da cadeia de construção. “Hoje, por conta desse volume, a energia é o fator preponderante para que esses projetos sejam conduzidos”, afirmou. A Elea estuda alternativas para diversificar suas fontes de energia e soluções de backup. Belchior esclareceu, entretanto, que a companhia não tem projeto de autoprodução em andamento. Nuvem, IA e repatriação de dados A diretora vê oportunidades de expansão entre grandes provedores de nuvem que poderão ampliar o processamento de inteligência artificial no Brasil. Esse movimento, segundo ela, pode combinar instalações próprias e contratação de provedores de colocation, conforme as necessidades de cada aplicação. Além da repatriação de dados processados no exterior, Belchior apontou a possibilidade de manter no país novas cargas decorrentes da digitalização de governos, instituições financeiras e outros setores. A executiva não estimou qual volume de dados poderia retornar ao Brasil. Na operação regional, a companhia também avalia a expansão do BSB2, em Brasília, e alternativas de aquisições ou investimentos na infraestrutura existente em Porto Alegre. Segundo Belchior, a estratégia combina projetos de grande escala com a ampliação da presença em mercados fora do eixo Rio–São Paulo.

artigo.texto: EU agrees higher allowance threshold for ETS reserve The Council of the European Union and the European Parliament reached a provisional agreement on 20 October 2026 on targeted changes to the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) market stability reserve. The agreement would increase the allowance invalidation threshold from 400 million to 700 million, subject to formal adoption. The reserve absorbs surplus emission allowances and can release allowances to address market imbalances. Since the invalidation mechanism began in 2023, more than 3 billion allowances had been removed. The Commission had proposed halting invalidation indefinitely, but the provisional agreement retained the mechanism with a higher threshold. The proposed higher threshold would retain a larger buffer for future market fluctuations, with the aim of improving liquidity and predictability while avoiding excessive oversupply. Implications for energy-intensive industry For pulp and paper producers, the proposal concerns the carbon-market framework affecting energy-intensive industry; it does not introduce a sector-specific measure. The Council said the additional reserve capacity could help respond to possible market tightness after the mid-2030s as the emissions cap declines. The institutions also agreed that a gradual reduction in the threshold should be included in the broader ETS review. Darragh O’Brien, Ireland’s Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment, said the agreement “provides European industry with immediate flexibility, while ensuring price stability and protecting the integrity of the EU carbon market”. Next steps The provisional text still requires endorsement by the Council and Parliament, followed by legal-linguistic revision and formal adoption. The amendment does not alter the overall design of the market stability reserve.

artigo.texto: Often hailed as a ‘dream battery’ due to its near-zero explosion risk and vastly expanded electric vehicle driving range, the solid-state battery is facing a shifting industry perspective. As commercialization draws closer, skepticism regarding profitability is mounting due to high costs and mass-production limitations. According to the battery industry, South Korea’s top three battery makers are all racing toward solid-state commercialization, but with varying degrees of urgency. Samsung SDI is currently pushing the hardest, targeting mass production by the second half of 2027. On the 6th of this month, the company signed a joint development agreement with battery material firm Ecopro BM for solid-state cathodes and solid electrolytes. A Samsung SDI official stated, “We are already supplying prototypes to clients and verifying performance. There are no changes in the demand from clients currently in discussions.” However, large-scale mass production will not begin immediately next year. The initial target markets are humanoid robots requiring fewer batteries and ultra-luxury electric vehicles capable of absorbing high battery costs. Yet, whether meaningful profits can be generated solely from supplying small quantities of batteries for robots and EVs remains uncertain. Industry watchers believe that given Samsung SDI’s long-standing dedication to solid-state development domestically, the move is intended to preempt a new market that even China has yet to dominate. In contrast, LG Energy Solution and SK On are adopting a more measured pace. LG Energy Solution has set its mass-production target for EV solid-state batteries in early 2029 and humanoid applications by 2030. A company official remarked, “We view solid-state batteries more as a ‘market extender’ that expands the market rather than an immediate ‘game changer’ that will replace it overnight.” This represents a more cautious stance compared to its self-published report last year, which heavily promoted solid-state technology as a future game-changer. Similarly, while SK On continues development after completing a solid-state pilot production line last year, it has scheduled commercialization for 2029 or later. Recently, the global EV market has seen low-cost Chinese LFP (lithium iron phosphate) batteries become mainstream, even with lower performance than ternary batteries. This background fuels concerns that high-priced solid-state batteries could face market rejection. Professor Lee Ho-keun of Daeduk University noted, “The question is how many cars can actually bear the cost of solid-state batteries. This now needs to be approached as an industrial issue rather than just a technological one, which won’t be easy in the short term.” Technological hurdles must also be cleared. Issues such as poor adhesion between solid materials, cracks during charging and discharging, and low production yields persist. An industry insider noted, “Making things in a laboratory and mass-producing them in a factory are entirely different challenges.” Skepticism is also surfacing in China. Ni Jun, Chief Manufacturing Officer (CMO) of CATL, the world’s largest battery company, stated last month, “The possibility of short-term commercialization for solid-state batteries is very low. Large-scale commercialization will take at least five years.” Chinese battery giants like CATL and BYD have likewise targeted commercialization around 2030. Nevertheless, experts emphasize that South Korea must claim the solid-state battery market first. Professor Park Chul-wan of Seojeong University stressed, “We have been talking about solid-state for decades; now is the time to prove the technology with actual products.” Professor Lee Sang-young of Yonsei University added, “Before China establishes solid-state standards and occupies the market, South Korea must create the benchmarks first and secure an early lead.” This implies finding a breakthrough in the solid-state sector through an “upgrading” strategy powered by technological prowess, escaping China’s onslaught of cheap battery supplies. Professor Kim Pil-soo of Daelim University pointed out, “Mass production is difficult, but the directional path of solid-state technology is correct. Domestic batteries struggling with price competition ultimately have no choice but to compete with high-value-added products.”

artigo.texto: Geely EX5 vs BYD Atto 3: Which EV Offers More? Table of Contents The Geely EX5 and BYD Atto 3 are two compact electric SUVs aimed at buyers looking for a practical family EV. The Geely EX5 has been showcased in Pakistan, but its local price and final specifications have not been announced. Meanwhile, the BYD Atto 3 is already available in the Pakistani market. To see how the two compare, we have taken the top-spec Thailand-market Geely EX5 and the Pakistan-spec BYD Atto 3 Advance, comparing their dimensions, motor performance, battery, charging, safety, and interior equipment. Quick Comparison Power 160 kW vs 150 kW Torque 320 Nm vs 310 Nm Battery 68.39 kWh vs 49.92 kWh Claimed Range 450 km WLTP vs 410 km NEDC DC Charging 20 min* vs 30 min Ground Clearance 173 mm vs 175 mm Infotainment 15.4 inches vs 15.6 inches All values follow Geely EX5 versus BYD Atto 3 order. *The EX5’s quoted DC charging time does not specify a charging percentage window. The Thai-spec EX5 offers a bigger battery and richer equipment, but Pakistan pricing will determine its value against the Atto 3. Dimensions The Geely EX5 is longer, wider and taller than the BYD Atto 3. It also has a longer wheelbase and slightly more boot space. The EX5 is 160 mm longer and 26 mm wider, with a 30 mm longer wheelbase. Its larger exterior dimensions provide more room for cabin packaging, although actual passenger space needs to be evaluated in person. The Atto 3 has a slightly higher ground clearance and a smaller turning radius. These differences could make it more convenient in tight parking areas and narrow streets. Motor and Performance The Geely EX5 has a 10 kW power advantage and produces 10 Nm more torque. It also accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h in 7.6 seconds, compared with 7.9 seconds for the Atto 3. However, the 0.3-second difference is relatively small. Both vehicles use front-wheel drive and should offer strong acceleration for daily city driving and highway overtaking. Battery, Range and Charging The Geely EX5’s 68.39 kWh battery is 18.47 kWh larger than the Atto 3’s 49.92 kWh battery. This represents approximately 37% more battery capacity. However, the claimed range figures follow different testing cycles. The EX5’s 450 km range uses WLTP, while the Atto 3’s 410 km figure follows NEDC. NEDC usually produces more optimistic range estimates than WLTP. Therefore, the advertised figures cannot be used to calculate the exact difference in real-world range. The EX5 also has a quoted 20-minute DC charging time, compared with approximately 30 minutes for the Atto 3 from 30% to 80%. However, the EX5’s charging window is not specified in the supplied data. Wheels and Tyres The Geely EX5 has larger 19-inch wheels and wider tyres. These give it a more substantial appearance and may provide greater tyre contact width. The Atto 3 uses 17-inch wheels with taller tyre sidewalls. This setup can offer advantages on uneven roads and potentially lower replacement costs, depending on tyre availability. Actual ride comfort will depend on suspension tuning, tyre construction and pressure, rather than wheel size alone. Exterior Features Both SUVs come with a pivotable panoramic sunroof, powered tailgate and surround-view cameras. The EX5 adds intelligent high-beam control and Follow-Me-Home lighting in the Thai specification. Its larger body also gives it a different road presence compared with the more compact Atto 3. Interior and Infotainment The Thai-spec Geely EX5 has the stronger interior technology package. Its 16-speaker Flyme Sound system, 13.8-inch head-up display and larger instrument cluster give it a clear equipment advantage. The BYD Atto 3 responds with a 15.6-inch rotating infotainment screen and a distinctive interior layout. For buyers who prioritize infotainment and audio equipment, the EX5 looks attractive on paper. However, Geely must confirm whether Pakistan will receive the same equipment. Comfort and Convenience Both SUVs have powered driver seats, electric tailgates and surround-view cameras. The final EX5 equipment list will determine whether these differences carry over to Pakistan. Safety Features Both SUVs offer important active safety systems, including automatic emergency braking, lane-keeping assistance and blind spot monitoring. The Atto 3 has seven airbags compared with six in the Thai-spec EX5. The EX5 also lists intelligent cruise control, collision mitigation systems and rear cross traffic braking. However, its supplied specification sheet describes 14 ADAS functions while listing only 13 abbreviations. The number of ADAS functions alone does not determine which vehicle is safer. Crash protection, system calibration and actual operating conditions also matter. Which One Looks More Practical for Pakistan? Geely EX5 (Thai Spec) - 68.39 kWh battery offers greater energy storage. - 461-litre boot provides more luggage space. - 173 mm ground clearance. - Premium equipment includes ventilated front seats and a 16-speaker audio system. - Pakistan price, local warranty and final specifications remain unconfirmed. BYD Atto 3 (Pakistan) - 49.92 kWh battery with a claimed 410 km NEDC range. - 440-litre boot and slightly higher ground clearance. - Smaller turning radius may help with city parking. - Published Pakistan-market equipment and ex-factory price. - Battery warranty of 8 years or 160,000 km. The EX5 offers more battery capacity, but local charging specifications and pricing remain unconfirmed. BYD Atto 3: Its known Pakistan price, confirmed specifications and smaller turning radius make it the more straightforward purchase today. artigo.texto: ASEIC Expands Carbon Market Cooperation with Vietnam Cooperation in Waste Heat Recovery, ESS, Solar Power, and Medical Waste Treatment The ASEM SMEs Eco-Innovation Center (ASEIC) said on October 27 that it held the opening ceremony of the 2026 Korea-Vietnam Eco-Innovation Partnership Week on October 26, attended by officials from the Department of Climate Change (DCC) at Vietnam’s Ministry of Agriculture and Environment. The program is part of ASEIC’s “Eco-Innovation Consulting and Capacity Building for Vietnamese SMEs” project. It was designed to strengthen Vietnam’s capacity to implement its carbon market system and expand cooperation between the two countries by sharing Korea’s policy and technological experience. At the opening ceremony, the DCC and ASEIC exchanged a letter of intent (LOI), and four Korean green technology companies signed memorandums of understanding (MOUs) with Vietnamese companies. Jeong Gwangcheon, chairman of ASEIC and president of the Korea Innovation Business Association, and Bui Duc Hieu, deputy director of the Department of Climate Change at Vietnam's Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, pose for a commemorative photo after exchanging a letter of intent (LOI) at the opening ceremony of the 2026 Korea-Vietnam Eco-Innovation Partnership Week on the 26th. ASEM SMEs Eco-Innovation Center View original image The agreements involved four Korean companies working in waste heat recovery and power generation; energy storage systems (ESS) and waste battery diagnostics; ESS and solar panels; and steam sterilization treatment of medical waste. ASEIC expects the agreements to expand opportunities for technology exchange and cooperation between companies in the two countries across various fields, including improving energy efficiency, using renewable energy, and managing waste. During their visit to Korea, Vietnamese officials plan to visit domestic institutions, including the Greenhouse Gas Inventory and Research Center of Korea (GIR) and the Korea Environment Corporation, to learn about Korea’s greenhouse gas management system and experience operating related policies and systems. They will also explore policy implications for implementing Vietnam’s carbon market system and ways for the two countries to cooperate.
