artigo.texto: Third-quarter profit growth slowed to 14.5%, fueled by competition from secondary manufacturers. According to the unaudited financial report submitted to the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on October 20, 2026, Contemporary Amperex Technology Limited (CATL) recorded operating revenue of 165.22 billion yuan (approximately US$24.74 billion) in the third quarter of 2026, a 58.58% increase year-on-year. Net profit attributable to parent company shareholders reached 21.25 billion yuan (approximately US$3.18 billion), a 14.54% increase compared to the third quarter of 2025. The gross profit margin for the period declined to 19.3%. Despite maintaining positive year-on-year growth, CATL's net profit growth rate in Q3 2026 slowed significantly compared to the 36% increase in Q2 2026 and the 57% increase recorded in Q4 2025. Simultaneously, both revenue and net profit figures for the past quarter were lower than the average forecast of analysts, which were RMB 175.05 billion in revenue and RMB 26.03 billion in net profit. Immediately after the financial results were released, CATL's stock fell by more than 10% on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange and 8.6% on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange during this week's trading sessions. The stock's decline has continued since September 2026, following the signing of supply agreements between domestic electric vehicle manufacturers Xiaomi and Li Auto and secondary battery producers. Besides market share competition, investor caution regarding the outlook for energy storage systems has also contributed to selling pressure, causing CATL's share price to fall by more than 20% on the Hong Kong market and 31% on the Shenzhen market since the beginning of 2026. For the first nine months of 2026, CATL's total operating revenue reached 442.14 billion yuan (approximately US$66.19 billion), a 56% increase compared to the same period in 2025. Net profit for the nine months reached 64.53 billion yuan (approximately US$9.66 billion), a 32% increase year-on-year. Research and development (R&D) expenses for the first three quarters were recorded at 18.52 billion yuan. Inventories rose 53% to over 144 billion yuan amid forecasts of slowing global battery demand in 2027. Amidst volatility in profit margins within China's electric vehicle industry, investment bank JPMorgan downgraded its Hong Kong-listed CATL stock rating to Neutral earlier this week. JPMorgan's report indicated that the re-imposition of consumption tax on battery products, the rollback of export tax refunds, and international trade barriers are creating significant costs for Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers, potentially dampening demand for CATL's battery products. However, the financial institution still believes CATL will maintain its leading position in terms of scale within the global battery industry. Sharing a cautious view on market prospects, in a report published in early October 2026, Citigroup forecasts that the growth rate of global battery consumption demand will decrease by 26% in 2027. This is due to the shrinking growth potential of the domestic electric vehicle market in China, combined with the slowdown in the energy storage system sector due to the high base level of the previous period. Regarding asset size and production expansion, as of September 30, 2026, CATL's inventory value reached 144.77 billion yuan (equivalent to US$21.68 billion), a 53% increase compared to the beginning of the year. The value of the group's ongoing infrastructure projects also increased by 45%, reaching 43 billion yuan (equivalent to US$6.44 billion). Company representatives explained that the increase in inventory and ongoing project costs was to support the plan to expand factory scale and enhance production capacity in the coming period. To support liquidity and stabilize stock prices on the stock market, earlier this week, CATL spent nearly 50 million yuan (approximately $7.49 million) to repurchase treasury shares listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. This transaction is part of the largest share buyback program in the company's history, with a total registered value of up to 40 billion yuan (equivalent to $6 billion) on the mainland stock market, announced in July 2026.

artigo.texto: A empresa de Elon Musk fechou um acordo de financiamento de 40 bilhões de dólares com a Apollo Global Management. O objetivo é comprar e alugar equipamentos de alta performance, como chips gráficos, para operar seus próprios centros de dados, com pagamentos ao longo de cinco anos. A SpaceX, a empresa espacial liderada pelo bilionário Elon Musk, acertou um acordo de financiamento no valor de cerca de 40 bilhões de dólares. O parceiro escolhido foi uma entidade administrada pela Apollo Global Management. O principal objetivo da operação é adquirir equipamentos avançados para a construção e operação de centros de dados próprios. Conforme documento oficial enviado nesta segunda-feira, 26, à Securities and Exchanges Commission (SEC), órgão regulador de mercados dos Estados Unidos, a transação prevê a compra de unidades de processamento gráfico (GPUs) e outros itens relacionados. A estratégia visa fortalecer a infraestrutura tecnológica da empresa para suportar operações de inteligência artificial e computação pesada. Detalhes do acordo e cronograma - O compromisso legal entre as partes foi assinado no dia 24 de outubro. - A entidade ligada à Apollo será responsável por comprar os equipamentos. - Depois, esses itens serão alugados pela Apollo para a SpaceX. - A SpaceX pagará valores trimestrais pela utilização da infraestrutura. - O período total dos contratos de arrendamento é de aproximadamente cinco anos. Como funcionará a entrega e o pagamento Os equipamentos não chegarão de uma só vez. A entrega ocorrerá em lotes distintos, seguindo um cronograma estabelecido. Os contratos individuais de aluguel estão previstos para começar a valer no primeiro semestre de 2027. Cada contrato terá uma duração que varia entre cinco anos e cinco anos e três meses, dependendo do lote específico. Sobre a parte financeira, a SpaceX confirmou que os pagamentos trimestrais serão feitos de forma antecipada. Em geral, cada parcela incluirá um vigésimo (1/20) do custo financiado do lote correspondente. Além disso, será acrescido um valor de juros, calculado sobre o saldo devedor a uma taxa anual fixa, que ainda será definida, bem como despesas adicionais. Impacto financeiro e formalização Os cálculos da SpaceX estimam que os pagamentos referentes ao principal do empréstimo totalizem aproximadamente 40 bilhões de dólares durante a vigência dos contratos. Este valor, no entanto, não inclui o montante dos juros nem outros custos operacionais que possam surgir. A empresa espera concluir a formalização final do acordo antes do fim de 2026, dependendo do cumprimento de determinadas condições preliminares.

artigo.texto: Rural Nevadans hate data centers. So why are their local governments doubling down on them? The debate over where data centers should be built in Nevada has exploded over the last year, with people across the state uniting against their construction in neighborhoods and urban areas. So when Lyon County's board of commissioners earlier this year advanced a company's request to move forward with construction of the Monarch Data Center on 500 acres of farmland just outside the county's seat, it raised a new question in the argument over where data centers do and don't belong. Should they be built on land historically dedicated to agricultural production? Rural Nevadans have overwhelmingly turned out at public meetings to say "no." "We don't want a data center here," David Janakos told the Lyon County commissioners in August. "Our town of Yerington has been lined up for a project we've never asked for." Until recently, Nevada's data centers have for the most part been tucked away in industrial parks. But research compiled by the Pew Research Center shows that more than two-thirds of roughly 1,500 data centers planned nationwide are slated to be built in rural areas and that nearly 40 percent of planned data centers are in counties that currently don't have any. In counties that are struggling financially, this could mean new revenue streams. "If you look at the tax revenue an industrial property brings in, it's significant," Lyon County Manager Andrew Haskin said. Doug Busselman, government affairs director at the Nevada Farm Bureau, said the Lyon County's board of commissioners' move to allow construction of a data center on farmland is an outlier — for the moment. But it doesn't mean Nevada's farmland and ranchland aren't vulnerable to being snapped up for development by data centers or other large industries. "There's no such thing as a good data center and no such thing as a bad data center," he said. "It's making sure you put the data center where it belongs and it fits in with the community." Lyon County is already pivoting from an economy based on agriculture to one centered more on industry. Yerington, the county seat, is an agricultural hub and home to one of the nation's leading onion producers, but in Fernley, the county's largest city, many residents commute to work at the nearby Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center in adjacent Storey County. Now, the county is on tap to have eight data centers built within its borders over the next several years, in part because of other infrastructure and industry development. The broader Northern Nevada region is ranked as one of the top locations in the world for data center construction. The massive Greenlink transmission line is being built through Lyon County, and NV Energy is constructing a substation as part of the project that is poised to be one of the largest in the world. Data center developers are looking to capitalize on that development, but it creates a tension between agriculture, industry and residents — a tension that has played out time and time again, according to Fred Steinmann, director of UNR's Center for Economic Development. "This is kind of the latest iteration of that." Money 'moves the needle in rural communities' Long a bedroom community and agricultural hub, Lyon County ranks dead last in the state for revenue per capita. According to data collected by Lyon County's comptroller, industry-heavy counties such as Storey and mining-heavy counties such as Eureka generate roughly 20 times the revenue per resident that Lyon County does. Even counties closer in population to Lyon outpace it — Nye County and Carson City generate two to two-and-a-half times the revenue per resident that Lyon County does. Nevada limits how much property tax can grow year over year. Because counties' revenue from farmlands generally comes from property taxes, it stifles the coffers of counties such as Lyon that have historically been driven by agriculture. Industry, however, not only pays property taxes, but sales and use taxes as well as business license fees. As development has proliferated around it, Lyon County has surged to become the third-largest county in the state by population. And as people move into the county, they require resources, whether that's maintained roads or law enforcement. "If residents aren't willing to pay 100 percent of the costs, you need industry to generate those revenues," Steinmann said. "Growth does not pay for itself." Patrick Donnelly, Great Basin director for the Center for Biological Diversity, said the data center surge in rural communities shows that developers are looking to capitalize on "small rural communities that are heavily influenced by relatively modest amounts of money. These are communities that are not used to infusions of millions of dollars." Steinmann said the issue is more nuanced. The same amount of money "moves the needle in rural communities" much further than it would in an urban area, he said. Like in other industries, data center developers are looking for reasonably priced land that has access to the grid, transportation infrastructure and an available workforce, Steinmann said. Lyon County checks a lot of those boxes. It's strategically located near the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center and has access to Interstate 80 and Highway 50, both of which run east to west, and Highway 95, which runs north to south. "Very few counties can point to all four directions," he said. "Lyon County is just kind of strategically positioned to be of interest to industry." According to a press release from Tract, a developer of data center campuses that last year acquired more than 1,000 acres of land in Lyon County, the Northern Nevada region "a compelling growth alternative to the Bay Area. Growth in the market is now starting to expand outward from the core data center activity in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center." artigo.texto: Publicidade A intensidade dos investimentos em inteligência artificial e a capacidade das companhias em gerar retorno financeiro tornaram-se temas centrais entre os investidores globais. Estrategistas da XP analisaram os aportes em capex das empresas do setor para mapear desafios operacionais, oportunidades e as melhores teses de posicionamento. - Esse conteúdo faz parte da newsletter semanal Expert Drops; saiba mais e se inscreva! Paralelamente, o avanço da infraestrutura necessária para suportar essa tecnologia impulsiona a demanda por data centers, segmento em que o Brasil apresenta forte potencial e no qual os fundos imobiliários podem atuar de forma relevante para ampliar o acesso dos investidores a esse mercado. Projeções do investimento massivo em inteligência artificial A corrida pela infraestrutura de inteligência artificial transforma as perspectivas do setor tecnológico, com estimativas indicando que os aportes das oito principais empresas americanas atinjam US$ 1,8 trilhão até o encerramento da década. Um levantamento detalhado analisa os reflexos desse ciclo intensivo de capital e os desdobramentos para as carteiras de investimento. Papel dos FIIs na expansão dos data centers A arrancada da inteligência artificial posiciona os data centers como pilar essencial do ecossistema de tecnologia, campo no qual o Brasil se destaca pela matriz elétrica limpa, capacidade energética e posição geográfica. O relatório detalha esse movimento e mostra como os fundos imobiliários começam a abrir pontes para o investidor acessar a tese de infraestrutura digital. Projeções conservadoras para o desempenho das companhias no 3T26 Diante de um contexto macroeconômico adverso tanto local quanto globalmente, a nova safra de balanços do terceiro trimestre de 2026 (3T26) tende a apresentar números contidos. As projeções consolidadas da equipe de estratégia indicam altas de 7,2% na receita líquida e 12% no EBITDA na comparação anual, enquanto o lucro líquido deve registrar estabilidade (+0,5%) nas empresas acompanhadas, revelando variações importantes entre as áreas analisadas. A expansão do cobre como pilar estratégico da Vale O crescimento na produção de cobre se consolida como ponto central da tese da Vale (VALE3), conforme avaliação após o Vale Base Metals Day e o Investor Tour no Canadá. Analistas da XP indicam que as reservas atuais sustentam a meta de atingir 700 quilotoneladas anuais até 2035, deslocando o foco principal das discussões da disponibilidade de recursos para a capacidade de execução dos projetos. Continua depois da publicidade Balanços das big techs nos EUA: resultados mistos no 3T26 A temporada de balanços nos Estados Unidos ganha tração com a divulgação de companhias ligadas à inteligência artificial. Análises de estratégia destacam um cenário heterogêneo: SpaceX e Meta superaram as projeções do consenso do mercado, enquanto a Tesla divulgou dados levemente desfavoráveis, pressionada pelo recuo do faturamento na divisão de energia. Fluxo financeiro internacional na Bolsa em outubro A injeção de capital de investidores internacionais na Bolsa local registrou forte avanço em outubro, somando R$ 10,1 bilhões no primeiro pregão após o 1º turno. O relatório mensal Fluxo em Foco analisa o potencial de continuidade desses aportes na renda variável, detalhando as posições e o espaço para novos ingressos caso o cenário otimista se confirme.

artigo.texto: O Brasil e a China estão a aprofundar a cooperação para desenvolver os seus mercados de carbono, através da partilha de experiências, da medição de emissões e da criação de mecanismos que apoiem a transição para uma economia de baixo carbono. A iniciativa foi destacada por Cristina Reis, secretária extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono do Ministério da Fazenda brasileiro, após participar numa conferência internacional realizada em setembro, em Wuhan. A China lançou o seu mercado regulado em 2021 e, até agosto de 2026, acumulava transações equivalentes a 961 milhões de toneladas de dióxido de carbono equivalente, avaliadas em 65,7 mil milhões de yuans. O país desenvolve também um mercado voluntário, no qual projetos podem gerar créditos de carbono. No Brasil, a Lei n.º 15.042, aprovada em dezembro de 2024, criou o Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões. A implementação decorre por etapas, incluindo a definição de regras para monitorizar, comunicar e verificar as emissões. A experiência chinesa poderá ajudar a aperfeiçoar estes procedimentos. A cooperação integra ainda a Coalizão Aberta para Mercados Regulados de Carbono, lançada na COP30, em Belém. Brasil, China e União Europeia lideram a iniciativa, que procura aproximar metodologias e regras entre sistemas nacionais. Um memorando bilateral sobre mercados de carbono poderá ser assinado na COP31, prevista para novembro, na Turquia.

artigo.texto: Oriente Médio é a região mais barata para construir data centers com a alta da demanda por IA O Oriente Médio ocupa a posição de região mais barata do mundo para a construção de data centers e, portanto, está bem posicionado para se beneficiar da migração para projetos de inteligência artificial em grande escala, segundo pesquisa da Turner & Townsend, empresa global de gestão de programas. O Data Centre Construction Index da companhia, agora em sua décima edição, compara custos de construção com base em mais de 500 projetos em andamento ou concluídos recentemente em 62 mercados, com o apoio de uma pesquisa com mais de 400 especialistas do setor. O estudo coloca a média do Oriente Médio em US$ 9,93 por watt, abaixo da Europa, com US$ 12,76, da Ásia, com US$ 12,10, e da América do Norte, com US$ 12,06. Três mercados do Oriente Médio aparecem entre as 62 localidades cobertas: a Arábia Saudita, com US$ 10,80, em 40º lugar; o Catar, com US$ 9,80, em 53º; e os Emirados Árabes Unidos, com US$ 9,20, em 58º. Alan Coary, diretor e responsável pela área de data centers no Oriente Médio da Turner & Townsend, atribuiu a posição da região a custos de construção e de energia comparativamente baixos, aliados a forte apoio governamental à infraestrutura de IA. Ele citou a iniciativa HUMAIN, da Arábia Saudita, e o investimento contínuo dos Emirados Árabes Unidos em IA e no desenvolvimento de data centers de hiperescala por meio da G42 e da Khazna como fatores que remodelam a capacidade computacional da região e sustentam sua ambição de ser um polo de IA competitivo globalmente, refletindo uma tendência mais ampla de IA soberana e de programas de infraestrutura digital apoiados por governos. No mundo, os custos de construção de data centers continuaram a subir em 2026, à medida que a demanda por capacidade computacional de IA e por projetos de grande escala superou a oferta de terrenos com energia disponível e de mão de obra qualificada. Embora a inflação global de custos tenha mostrado alguma estabilização em 2026, custos e riscos de construção estruturalmente mais altos vêm sendo cada vez mais precificados nos contratos, enquanto a escassez crescente de qualificação aumenta a pressão sobre os custos de mão de obra. A alta dos custos é cada vez mais impulsionada pela escala crescente das obras, sobretudo das instalações de IA, que exigem abordagens alternativas de entrega, especialistas técnicos e novos modelos de equilíbrio de riscos para aliviar a capacidade sobrecarregada e acelerar os cronogramas. Entre os entrevistados, 52% esperam que a maior parte de seus projetos de 2027 sejam data centers que atendam a cargas de trabalho de IA. Além disso, 52% relataram aumentos de custos acima de 6% em 2026, e cerca de 20% citaram inflação acima de 15%. Para 2027, 28% dos entrevistados globais esperam inflação entre 1% e 5%, o que indica continuidade do arrefecimento da pressão de custos, e 57% esperam inflação abaixo de 15%. A energia foi apontada como um dos principais obstáculos à entrega bem-sucedida por 56% dos entrevistados, com 52% relatando que as conexões à rede elétrica costumam levar de um a dois anos e 32% relatando prazos superiores a dois anos. As localidades mais caras do índice foram Tóquio, com US$ 18,28; Osaka, com US$ 17,15; Zurique, com US$ 15,93; Singapura, com US$ 15,39; e o Vale do Silício, com US$ 15,01. O Japão ocupa o primeiro lugar, enquanto 17 mercados europeus e 13 norte-americanos compõem quase metade da tabela principal, refletindo a contínua dominância dessas regiões. Cerca de metade de todos os data centers do mundo está na América do Norte, e um quarto, na Europa. As localidades mais baratas foram Xangai, com US$ 5,79; Mumbai, com US$ 6,83; Cidade de Ho Chi Minh, com US$ 8,32; Bogotá, com US$ 9,13; e os Emirados Árabes Unidos, com US$ 9,20. Esses mercados emergentes oferecem mão de obra mais barata e maior acesso a ela. Paul Barry, responsável pelo índice de custos de construção na Turner & Townsend, disse que o setor se transformou ao longo da década desde a primeira publicação do índice, com o investimento de capital em data centers agora em US$ 800 bilhões por ano e expectativa de chegar a US$ 1,8 trilhão até 2050. Ele afirmou que a rápida demanda da IA por capacidade computacional, combinada à adoção da nuvem e à importância crescente dos dados e da capacidade soberana, impulsiona investimentos e desenvolvimento em escala sem precedentes e remodela o cenário da construção. Ele também observou que o aumento dos custos de materiais e de mão de obra continua a criar desafios em todo o mundo, enquanto o acesso a energia, a equipamentos especializados e a qualificação segue como gargalo. Os data centers enfrentam escrutínio crescente, o que torna o consentimento político e das comunidades essencial para a entrega, e a demanda impulsionada pela IA por energia em nível de gigawatt e por resfriamento líquido para maiores densidades de rack alimenta projetos de maior escala, enquanto a escassez de mão de obra qualificada e os maiores riscos na entrega de projetos mais complexos impõem um prêmio de custo.

artigo.texto: MaxVolt Energy Showcases Energy Storage and EV Battery Portfolio at REI Expo 2026 MaxVolt Energy presented its rack-type energy storage systems, lithium inverter batteries and EV battery packs on the opening day of REI Expo 2026. October 26, 2026. By News Bureau MaxVolt Energy Industries showcased its energy storage and electric mobility battery portfolio on the opening day of the 19th edition of the Renewable Energy India Expo (REI Expo) 2026 in Greater Noida. The company presented its rack-type ESS from 4.8 kWh to 60 kWh for homes, solar installations and Commercial and Industrial (C&I) sites, with battery life of up to 10 years. Alongside these were lithium inverter batteries, MaxVolt’s storage inverters, solar batteries and lithium battery packs for electric two-wheelers and three-wheelers. Together they showcased MaxVolt’s range across both renewable storage and electric mobility. Mukesh Gupta, Co-Founder and Chief Marketing Officer, MaxVolt Energy Industries, said, “REI Expo is where the people building India’s renewable future come looking for partners they can rely on. Our message this year is clear: MaxVolt makes storage for every scale, from a home to a factory floor, alongside the EV batteries our partners already know us for. Our dealers and OEM partners have taken us to 22 states. The conversations at our stall, with installers, EPC firms and distributors, tell us the market is ready to move from lead-acid to lithium, and we are ready to meet it.” REI Expo brings India’s solar and storage ecosystem under one roof, and this year storage is central to that conversation. As solar capacity grows, battery storage is what makes renewable power usable round the clock. The Central Electricity Authority projects India will need about 208 GWh of battery storage by 2029-30. MaxVolt’s showcase answers that need directly: storage that works with solar, from a single home to a factory floor. Bhuvneshwar Pal Singh, Managing Director and Chief Financial Officer, MaxVolt Energy Industries Limited, added, “FY26 gave us a strong base. As we move through the second half of FY27, our focus is disciplined, profitable growth: making full use of our Duhai capacity, deepening our dealer and OEM network, and building Aligarh in phases so that new capacity comes up in step with demand. Energy storage is a growing part of that plan, and we expect it to play a larger role in our business in the years ahead.” The company has been manufacturing since 2019 and now runs a 2.5 GWh plant at Duhai, Ghaziabad. The company reported FY26 revenue of INR 296.8 crore, up 176 percent year on year, with profit after tax of INR 24.4 crore. Its network covers 950 plus dealers and 170 plus OEM partners across 22 states. In September 2026, MaxVolt held the bhoomi poojan for a planned 10 GWh plant at Khyamai Industrial Estate, Aligarh. The plant represents an investment of INR 700 crore and will be built in two phases of 5 GWh each. When complete, it will take the company’s total capacity to 12.5 GWh and is expected to create 1,500 to 2,000 direct jobs. The plant is designed to meet growing demand across all of MaxVolt’s segments, including dedicated lines for OEM partners. The company’s roadmap also includes a planned entry into four-wheeler EV batteries and continued Battery Management System (BMS) research with IIT Roorkee. Through its recycling subsidiary, MaxVolt ReEarth, the company is building a circular approach to the batteries it makes. please contact: contact@energetica-india.net.

artigo.texto: Dubuque County targets traffic, emergency strain as data center debate looms over election DUBUQUE, Iowa (KCRG) - Dubuque County leaders want to make sure developers, not local taxpayers, pay for busy roads and strained emergency services if large data centers break ground in the area. During a dedicated work session Monday, the Dubuque County Board of Supervisors questioned local law enforcement to determine how narrow secondary roads and emergency crews would survive years of industrial construction. The discussions come as the county nears the November election, with Supervisor Ann McDonough not seeking re-election at the end of her term and incumbent Wayne Kenniker on the ballot. Dubuque County is several months into a one-year moratorium on large-scale facilities, giving officials until next July to craft a binding regulatory ordinance. Sheriff Joe Kennedy told supervisors his review of other Iowa communities with active data centers showed that once operating, the facilities rarely require police assistance. “Once the construction is complete, there’s a limited number of people that actually work inside the facilities,” Kennedy said. “The actual issues that they have on site once the thing’s operational are pretty minimal.” The disruption, Kennedy noted, comes during the building process, when hundreds of workers, heavy machinery, and constant material deliveries descend onto two-lane county routes like Sundown Road. “When it comes to the traffic, it’s really going to depend on what the scope of the project is,” Kennedy said. “At the entrances we’re probably going to have an increased number of rear-end accidents and things like that.” To prevent public deputies from being pulled from regular patrols, Kennedy urged supervisors to write rules requiring developers to pay for off-duty law enforcement to direct traffic. “Obviously, we have limited resources, so it’s not like we can just go down there and send our people down there all day on duty and tie them up all day with that,” Kennedy said. “I think that it’s a small cost for these data center companies to ensure that they have safe operations going in and out of there.” That friction on rural roadways is already hitting home for neighbors. During public comments, resident Mary Beth Decker explained that harvest traffic already makes walking along rural routes a hazard. “I had to give that up because the semis, the tractors, and things going down there became too dangerous,” Decker said. “I had to make a different route...especially during harvest time.” McDonough pointed out that draft proposals limiting construction to daytime hours and weekdays will compress traffic into tight windows, creating logistical headaches. “There’s not night shifts to this for construction. And there’s no weekend construction, at least that’s the draft. So it’s going to be a resource issue,” McDonough said. She stressed that dropping a massive campus into a rural area demands intensive preparation before a shovel moves. “This isn’t like somebody gives you a flyer and says they’re going to be open on Monday,” McDonough said. “There’s close coordinated communication about how something this big would roll.” Monday’s focus on roads adds to months of mounting testimony at the courthouse. Last month, public health officials urged supervisors to adopt strict decibel caps, warning that continuous noise from cooling systems and server fans causes chronic stress, elevated blood pressure, and sleep disruption. Residents have also raised concerns over local landfill capacity, asking whether regional sites could handle large volumes of demolition and electronic waste. McDonough’s decision not to seek re-election means the county will swear in at least one new supervisor in January as the board continues working toward a final ordinance. Dubuque County’s moratorium runs through July 2027, with supervisors scheduled to address water consumption, cooling systems, and groundwater protections at upcoming sessions. Copyright 2026 KCRG. O Google (GOGL34) teria derrubado mais de 250 mil árvores na cidade de Muhos, no interior da Finlândia, de forma irregular. A big tech planeja construir um data center no local da plantação. De acordo com reportagem do jornal The Guardian, a empresa não teria autorização do governo para tal ação. Estima-se que o total represente até um quarto da área de 300 hectares de floresta. O governo ordenou que a empresa norte-americana interrompa imediatamente o projeto de data center. Além disso, a comunidade local saiu em defesa da área atingida e pede um debate amplo sobre o assunto. Pouco depois de o caso vir a público, o diretor do Google para a Finlândia, Antti Järvinen, se pronunciou pedindo desculpas pelo corte das árvores. Ele, porém, defendeu que a empresa teria atuado “com base no melhor entendimento que tínhamos da legislação na época”. Leia mais: Bradesco (BBDC4) lucra R$ 7,1 bilhões, mas ações caem após balanço Essa não é a primeira área desmatada pelo Google na Finlândia. Em Otanmäki, a empresa também derrubou 150 mil árvores para construir outro data center. “A princípio, não consegui acreditar. Nunca ouvi falar de nenhuma empresa que tenha feito algo assim na Finlândia”, disse Hanna Halmeenpää, presidente do conselho da Associação Finlandesa pela Conservação da Natureza, à reportagem. “Eles compraram uma vasta área de terra e simplesmente começaram a desmatá-la, assim, sem mais nem menos. É pura arrogância e é inacreditável”. Data center na Amazônia A construção de novos data centers pelo mundo vem da necessidade de infraestrutura para a inteligência artificial. E isso não é exclusividade de países desenvolvidos. No Brasil, está em marcha o projeto BEL 1, que prevê a construção de um espaço dentro da Amazônia. A proposta é uma parceria da Elea Data Centers com a Axia Energia. Diversos órgãos ambientais denunciam que o projeto está em andamento sem os devidos licenciamentos ambientais. Além disso, o projeto também alimenta o debate sobre as chamadas “ilhas de calor”, que superaquecem o ambiente urbano, já que elevam a temperatura externa. A empresa que constrói o data center, porém, diz que vai usar sistemas de ar condicionado para resfriar os equipamentos. Além disso, [o texto original termina aqui com uma frase incompleta.] "Quando se constrói um data center maior, eu penso que essa sugestão de ouvir a sociedade tem que ser vista. Nesta fase eu posso garantir que não tem nenhum impacto. Será como um shopping center de médio porte, que ainda consome muito mais calor do que um data center deste tamanho na fase inicial", afirma o fundador e CEO da Elea, o italiano Alessandro Lombardi. Alphabet (GOGL34) sobe gastos de capital para até US$ 205 bilhões em 2026, por conta da IA.

artigo.texto: CATL's Buyback Arithmetic Meets the Margin Test Published on 10/25/2026 at 15:01 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL shares jumped 7.8% on Friday, snapping a seven-session losing streak as Chinese equities, automakers and battery names rallied together. Reuters linked the broader advance to a burst of trading in exchange-traded funds favoured by state-linked investors, while media reports tied CATL's move to share buybacks. No single catalyst has been confirmed for the gain. The scale of the rebound matters less than what comes next. The real question for investors is whether CATL can convert its formidable revenue growth back into convincing profit — a buyback supports that case but cannot substitute for operational proof. A Buyback With a Cancellation Clause The company's repurchase programme carries an unusual detail: the bought-back shares are to be cancelled, with registered capital reduced accordingly. That resolution covers a announced plan, not a completed buyback. Separately, a mandatory disclosure documents a specific purchase on 19 October, when CATL bought back A-shares for RMB 49,993,616.4. That transaction has already been executed and should not be conflated with the planned total volume. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? CATL also put real money behind its stock during the recent slump. On Wednesday it repurchased 3.4886 million A-shares for close to RMB 800 million, according to a filing published Thursday. In Hong Kong, the stock recovered alongside the wider market and a raft of auto names, ending seven consecutive days of losses. Revenue Surges, Profit Lags Tuesday's quarterly report laid bare the tension at the heart of the investment case. Third-quarter 2026 revenue reached RMB 165.221 billion, up 58.6% year on year. Net profit attributable to shareholders came in at RMB 21.246 billion, a gain of 14.54%. Reuters reported that analysts had expected profit growth of 41.2%. The disappointment was therefore not a decline in earnings but a sharply missed pace of expansion — and it was this shortfall, according to Reuters, that triggered the severe sell-off after the numbers. The cash picture adds another cautionary note. Operating cash flow for the first nine months of 2026 fell 23.60% compared with the prior year, meaning the inflow from day-to-day business shrank even as quarterly profit rose. JPMorgan downgraded CATL to "Neutral" on Wednesday, with media reports citing concerns about fading profitability in China's electric-vehicle industry. The broker's price target was cut to HK$500 from HK$725, reflecting a faster-than-expected deterioration in battery-sector margins. Swap Orders Offer a Counterweight Against that backdrop, CATL's battery-swapping business provides the most tangible offset. The company said Tuesday it had secured orders for swap products covering 13,000 vehicles, naming logistics clients SF Holding and China Postal Express & Logistics among the buyers. Such orders give the expansion a firmer footing than product announcements alone. CATL also plans to build out its battery-swap network for heavy trucks. Should those orders translate into profitable business and the network pull in further demand, they could counterbalance competitive pressure. The standardized swap blocks unveiled Tuesday were presented with fewer components and lower costs. According to the company, component count drops 52% versus existing products, while costs are set to come in 15% lower. Those figures describe product-level advantages; they do not yet prove a corresponding improvement in group profit. In the bull case, however, such cost savings would make additional volume more economically attractive — a more meaningful driver for valuation than the number of new product variants. CATL at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Competition Could Cap the Upside The bear case is equally concrete. Reuters identified fierce competition in the battery market and cooling Chinese car sales as the backdrop to the weaker profit growth. Either could prevent large revenue gains from producing a comparable lift in earnings. Buybacks do nothing to solve that operational problem. They change neither the competitive landscape nor the earnings quality of new orders, and a larger swap network does not automatically guarantee attractive margins. If CATL is forced to pass cost advantages on to customers, volumes could rise without profit growth accelerating enough to satisfy the market. Until CATL can back its revenue growth with firm orders and lower product costs, an operational basis for recovery remains intact. It would become far more convincing if those gains showed up in profit. Should the weaker earnings momentum instead become entrenched, Friday's advance would look like little more than a technical bounce after the losses. The next tangible test is execution: turning the secured swap-product orders into revenue and expanding the truck-swap network as planned. Progress there could shore up the growth story; a re-rating would require it to be economically convincing as well. Orders, cost cuts and buybacks demonstrate what the company can do — but the missed profit expectations show that growth alone is not enough. Profitability must supply the next piece of evidence. artigo.texto: Crea e FIERN articulam polo de data centers e cobram avanço de cabos submarinos Documento apresentado nesta sexta-feira (23), durante conferência na FIERN, propõe segurança jurídica e incentivos para novos empreendimentos; implantação de cabos submarinos ainda depende de definições federais. Resumo da Notícia - O Crea-RN lançou a Carta de Natal, um pacto para atrair investimentos em centros de processamento de dados, durante a Data Center Conference realizada nesta sexta-feira (23), na FIERN. - O documento reúne propostas de segurança jurídica, licenciamento ambiental e medidas tributárias para ampliar a competitividade do Rio Grande do Norte. - A abundância de energia renovável é apontada como vantagem, mas o estado ainda enfrenta desafios relacionados à conectividade internacional e à infraestrutura de transmissão. - O pacto não representa contratos de investimento já firmados. As propostas de incentivos fiscais e a instalação de cabos submarinos ainda dependem de decisões e medidas posteriores. O Rio Grande do Norte deu um novo passo na tentativa de atrair investimentos em infraestrutura digital nesta sexta-feira (23), com o lançamento da “Carta de Natal”, um pacto voltado à instalação de data centers no estado. O documento foi apresentado durante a Data Center Conference 2026, realizada na sede da Federação das Indústrias do Rio Grande do Norte (FIERN), em Natal, reunindo representantes dos setores de tecnologia, energia, engenharia e desenvolvimento econômico. A iniciativa é liderada pelo Conselho Regional de Engenharia e Agronomia do Rio Grande do Norte (Crea-RN), em articulação com instituições como FIERN e Sebrae. O objetivo é construir condições para receber empreendimentos de processamento e armazenamento de dados, com regras estáveis de licenciamento, segurança jurídica e propostas de incentivos tributários. O documento foi apresentado ao Instituto de Desenvolvimento Sustentável e Meio Ambiente (Idema) e ao Parque Científico e Tecnológico Augusto Severo (PAX), vinculado à UFRN, cujos representantes demonstraram abertura à colaboração. A assinatura do pacto, entretanto, não representa a confirmação de investimentos, contratos ou implantação imediata de novos empreendimentos. Acompanhe o Portal N10 no Google Escolha o N10 entre suas fontes preferidas para encontrar nossas notícias. Uma das principais vantagens apontadas pelo setor produtivo é a capacidade de geração de energia renovável do RN. O estado produz eletricidade em quantidade superior à demanda local e enfrenta restrições de escoamento em determinados períodos, situação conhecida como curtailment. A instalação de grandes consumidores, como data centers, é apontada como uma alternativa para aproveitar parte dessa produção. O presidente do Crea-RN, Roberto Wagner Costa, destacou que a abundância energética precisa ser acompanhada de investimentos na infraestrutura elétrica. “Isso exigirá planejamento da transmissão, subtransmissão, subestações e pontos de conexão”, afirmou. Segundo ele, o consumo de energia pelos novos empreendimentos também poderia ampliar a arrecadação estadual. RN ainda depende de avanços na conexão por cabos submarinos Apesar da disponibilidade de energia, o Rio Grande do Norte enfrenta um obstáculo importante para receber grandes centros de processamento: a conectividade internacional. Durante a conferência, especialistas destacaram a necessidade de ampliar a infraestrutura de fibra óptica, especialmente por meio de cabos submarinos capazes de transportar grandes volumes de informações entre o Brasil e outros países. A secretária-adjunta de Desenvolvimento Econômico do RN, Emília Casanova, informou que existem estudos de viabilidade para áreas de conexão na costa potiguar, mas ainda falta uma definição oficial do Ministério das Comunicações. Entre as possibilidades discutidas estão Natal e a região da Costa Branca. O Governo do Estado já havia apresentado ao Governo Federal projetos para receber data centers e cabos submarinos, incluindo a delimitação de 11 áreas prioritárias no litoral potiguar. A proposta busca ampliar a conexão do estado às redes internacionais, hoje fortemente concentradas no Ceará. O presidente da FIERN, Roberto Serquiz, defende que a proximidade com a infraestrutura existente no estado vizinho pode favorecer a expansão para o RN. A implantação, porém, depende de definições técnicas, investimentos e articulação com o Governo Federal. Pacto prevê discussão de incentivos fiscais e regras para novos investimentos A Carta de Natal, divulgada oficialmente pelo Crea-RN, também aborda propostas em estudo nas secretarias estaduais de Tributação e Desenvolvimento Econômico, incluindo a possível desoneração do ICMS sobre a energia consumida pelos empreendimentos e a redução de tributos incidentes sobre a importação de equipamentos. Essas medidas ainda dependem das etapas legais necessárias à sua implementação. O estado já avançou na regulamentação ambiental do setor, com a aprovação, pelo Conselho Estadual do Meio Ambiente (Conema), de critérios para o licenciamento de data centers, considerando capacidade elétrica, sistemas de refrigeração e possíveis impactos ambientais. A conferência também reuniu representantes da Associação Brasileira de Data Centers, do Banco do Nordeste, da Neoenergia Cosern, da Potigás e de empresas de infraestrutura. A programação oficial incluiu debates sobre financiamento, conectividade, eficiência energética e oportunidades para fornecedores locais. A coordenação das próximas articulações ficará com o HUB Crea-RN, que exercerá a função de secretaria executiva do movimento. O pacto permanece aberto à adesão de outras instituições, enquanto a atração de empreendimentos dependerá do avanço das condições regulatórias, da infraestrutura e das negociações com investidores.

artigo.texto: Finance first, batteries twice: what India's DISCOMs will discuss at DUM 2026 India Smart Grid Forum's 10th Distribution Utility Meet runs October 27-28, 2026 in Jaipur, with senior officials from 40+ power distribution companies expected. The first session covers distributor finances and capital market readiness. Two of the seven sessions name battery storage. This story was produced through MarketScale. See how Energy teams put it to work with Customer Stories & Case Studies. Key takeaways Two of DUM 2026's seven sessions name battery storage, and finance and capital-market readiness is listed first: India's distributors are putting the hardware and the money on the same two-day program. ISGF’s event page records 688 participants and 45-plus DISCOMs at the 2025 Mumbai edition, a baseline suppliers can use when judging whether DUM reaches DISCOM decision-makers. Free workspace Turn your Energy expertise into content. Record interviews, organize footage, and write with AI on a free trial of the MarketScale platform for qualifying companies. No demo required, no credit card. The first session at India's 10th Distribution Utility Meet is about money: DISCOM financial transformation and capital market readiness. Two of the seven sessions on the program name battery storage outright. Senior officials from 40+ DISCOMs across India are expected at the two-day event in Jaipur, which opens on October 27. The 10th Distribution Utility Meet will take place on 27-28 October 2026 in Jaipur, Rajasthan, with India Smart Grid Forum (ISGF) as organizer. According to ISGF, the host utilities are all three of Rajasthan's distribution companies, or DISCOMs: Jaipur Vidyut Vitran Nigam (JVVNL), Jodhpur Vidyut Vitran Nigam (JdVVNL) and Ajmer Vidyut Vitran Nigam (AVVNL). The event is supported by the Ministry of Power, NITI Aayog, Rajasthan's energy department, the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) and the All India DISCOMs Association (AIDA). Taken together, the agenda suggests what is on distributors' desks: paying for upgrades, storage on local grids and large new loads. That could make it useful to anyone who sells into Indian distribution networks or plans for them. The meet's theme, according to trade outlet Exhibition Showcase, is "Collaborative Growth." Seven sessions, two on batteries Over two days, the meet will hold seven thematic sessions: - DISCOMs financial transformation and capital market readiness - Scaling digital intelligence and advanced smart meter data analytics - How renewables can help handle new and emerging loads while keeping supply reliable and power quality high - CEA standards for solar PV and BESS, along with flexibility solutions for distribution networks - Climate resilience and securing the physical assets of DISCOMs - India Energy Stack, data exchange framework, cyber security and data privacy for digital grids - BESS applications in power distribution: select case studies Storage turns up twice. It sits beside distribution-network flexibility and the CEA's standards for solar PV and battery energy storage systems (BESS), then gets a session built entirely on case studies. Renewables get a third slot, framed around new and emerging loads and keeping supply reliable and power quality steady. Session 2 is Scaling Digital Intelligence and Advanced Smart Meter Data Analytics, which suggests a focus on using meter data. Finance leads the running order, ahead of every technology topic on the list. Exhibition Showcase likewise expects the conference to cover utility performance and the financial sustainability of DISCOMs alongside grid modernisation and digitalisation. For a supplier, that ordering suggests the conversation about any upgrade may start with how it gets paid for. In the announcement, ISGF president Reji Kumar Pillai tied these themes together. He said utilities are moving "from turnaround to transformation" as their networks take on smart meters, distributed renewables and storage, along with large new loads like AI data centres and EVs. That change, he said, gives peer learning among DISCOM leaders more value. Read beside a first session on capital market readiness, Pillai's "transformation" framing suggests finance is still part of the job, not a chapter that closed with the turnaround. The technology on his list, from smart meters to storage, maps directly onto sessions 2, 4 and 7. For suppliers selling solar PV equipment, battery systems or meter-data software into Indian distribution networks, sessions 2, 4, 6 and 7 could be the most relevant. Session 2 is the meter-data slot. Session 4 covers the CEA standards. Session 6 covers the India Energy Stack (IES), the data exchange framework, cyber security and data privacy for digital grids, topics that could shape how DISCOMs choose digital grid products. India Smart Grid Forum describes itself as a think-tank on energy transition, electric mobility and grid modernization. It was set up in 2011 as a public-private partnership initiative of the Government of India and is registered as a not-for-profit society in New Delhi. It has run DUM since 2017 around the objective of "Experience Sharing and Learning from Each Other." Who fills the hall in Jaipur ISGF expects more than 500 participants this year, including senior officials from 40+ DISCOMs and more than 100 speakers from utilities, regulators, policy bodies, research groups and technology providers. The 9th edition, which took place in Mumbai on 04-05 November 2025, is the obvious baseline. ISGF's event page records it this way. artigo.texto: African governments are developing policies to manage waste from solar panels, batteries and other clean tech equipment as installations surge, with officials warning the energy transition could create a new environmental problem unless it is accompanied by investment in recycling and reuse. Many African households and businesses are increasingly turning away from unreliable grid power or deciding not to wait for access, and are installing more solar panels and battery storage. Data from energy think-tank Ember, published in August, projects that the continent will install a record 17 gigawatts (GW) of solar capacity in 2026 - equal to around 100,000 solar panels every day. This would mark the third consecutive year of record growth, following increases of 51% in 2025 and 25% in 2024. While generally a welcome sign of progress towards a cleaner energy mix, this trend could also create a headache for African officials. Anselm Marungu, Namibia’s deputy minister of environment, forestry and tourism, believes rules should be put in place to ensure that valuable materials can be recovered from discarded solar panels, batteries and inverters at the end of their useful life. artigo.texto: A data center is often discussed as a digital asset. Itâs also a physical one: a major site that depends on power, electrical equipment, and a connection to the grid. That matters as UK Chancellor John Healey prepares to deliver his first budget on Oct. 28, with the government planning to give mayors a larger share of business rates from April 2027. The case for devolution is clear. Places that attract investment should share in its benefits. But the way that investment is taxed will shape where projects go, what infrastructure gets built, and whether promised capacity can be delivered. Business rates are a recurring property tax, calculated by applying a multiplier to a propertyâs rateable value. For data centers, valuation can include plant and machinery as well as the building. Most pay the higher multiplier for the most valuable properties. This yearâs revaluation increased rateable values at prime sites in London and Slough by between a quarter and a half. If local mayors retain more of the resulting revenue, a data center can become a substantial continuing addition to a regionâs tax base. That creates a direct incentive to attract projects and potentially offer rate relief to win them. Devolving business rates therefore can become a form of tax competition: regions forgoing revenue today in the hope of collecting more tomorrow. The danger is that while tax policy can influence a developerâs choice of location, it canât create the power needed to operate the site. A tax break can bring a project to the table but not deliver a grid connection. The US offers a stark warning. States spent a decade using sales-tax exemptions to attract data centers and, this year, lawmakers in two dozen states tried to repeal or reduce them after costs exceeded forecasts. In Virginia, the cost reached about 16 times the original estimate. Tax relief can lower a developerâs bill, but if a site canât get power, the public bears the cost without securing the investment or capacity the incentive was meant to support. The UK budget should set a clear test for business-rate relief. Whether offered by local councils or mayors, it should be conditional on grid readiness â a firm connection date or capacity reserved in an AI growth zone. Relief should be linked to delivery milestones, with a review or clawback if a project fails to proceed on time. The tax benefit should follow progress on the ground, not simply a developerâs choice of location. A national framework would help avoid regions competing through increasingly generous packages. It should define connection readiness and delivery milestones, and require government to publish the expected and actual cost of relief. Business-rate discounts and capital allowances need to be assessed separately. A rate discount reduces local receipts while it applies; a capital allowance changes when a company can deduct qualifying investment from taxable profits. The budget should use capital allowances to support the grid infrastructure developers are starting to fund themselves. In AI growth zones, developers may be able to build their own substations and high-voltage lines where that gets them connected sooner. These assets can add capacity the network would otherwise need to fund and help ease constraints beyond a single data center site. Qualifying special-rate expenditure generally can now receive a 50% first-year allowance, with the remaining balance written down at 6% on a declining balance basis. A qualifying main-rate plant can receive a 100% first-year allowance. Electrical equipment around data centers may fall into either category, depending on its classification and use. The chancellor should consider extending a 100% first-year allowance to qualifying private substations and connection assets. Bringing tax relief forward would improve project cash flow and reduce the tax penalty on developers who invest in infrastructure that adds network capacity. It wouldnât be a cash grant; its fiscal cost would depend on the qualifying investment and the timing of deductions. Eligibility should depend on an assetâs contribution to connection, not simply its location inside a data center site. Power equipment is another constraint. Switchgear, transformers, and protection equipment can take months or years to arrive because manufacturers are fully booked. A targeted allowance or credit for investment in UK production capacity could support data centers, housing, transport, and other electrification projects. It should reward additional capacity, with clear eligibility and a measurable fiscal cost. These proposals should be judged on whether they change the location, timing, or scale of investment enough to justify the revenue forgone. Relief that only changes the timing of a project that was already proceeding may have little additional effect. Fiscal discipline and infrastructure delivery should be considered together. A data centerâs value is measured in megawatts. Tax policy should follow the power, not the location. Get the balance wrong, and regions may compete for projects the grid canât serve. Get it right, and tax relief can steer investment to available power, encourage developers to add capacity and help build the supply chain that Britainâs wider electrification depends on. artigo.texto: Principais Conclusões - Elon Musk disse no sábado que espera ver muito poder de computação ocioso em data centers parcialmente concluídos. - Esse risco recai sobre as neoclouds como CoreWeave e Nebius, que compraram GPUs antes dos prédios para operá-las, e o CEO da NVIDIA diz que a escassez de capital já está desacelerando suas construções. - A CoreWeave pagou $1,2 bilhão de juros líquidos em 2025 contra uma perda operacional de $46 milhões, portanto não tem lucro para absorver um local paralisado. - O relatório da CoreWeave de 12 de novembro mostrará se sua potência ativa está alcançando os 4,2 gigawatts que contratou. CoreWeave (CRWV) perdeu mais de um terço de seu valor em outubro, conforme seus títulos caíram devido a temores sobre a dívida. Agora, Elon Musk deu aos acionistas mais um motivo para se preocupar. O cofundador da Hyperbolic, Yuchen Jin, publicou no X o que ouviu de um "amigo de neolab" que garantiu capacidade de GPU antecipadamente: "Os preços de aluguel de H100/B200/B300 desde então subiram 2–3x. Podemos simplesmente revender o poder de computação e imprimir dinheiro." A resposta de Musk no sábado: "Acho que vamos ver muito poder de computação ocioso em data centers parcialmente concluídos." Isso é um problema para quem comprou os chips antes do prédio estar pronto. Uma GPU em um local pela metade não gera receita, enquanto a dívida que a pagou continua custando juros. Esse risco está com as neoclouds como CoreWeave e Nebius (NBIS), que compraram capacidade antes dos prédios para operá-la. O TIKR acompanha 42 analistas da CoreWeave. Quantos dizem "Comprar"? Veja a distribuição completa das recomendações de Compra, Manter e Venda para a CoreWeave, junto com as estimativas de receita e lucro de Wall Street, tudo em um só lugar. Mais de 500.000 investidores usam o TIKR para pesquisar ações como esta. Veja as Recomendações dos Analistas para a CoreWeave Cada peça precisa aparecer Musk explicou o porquê em outra resposta no mesmo dia. Ele estava respondendo a uma publicação que listava o que limita a energia para data centers: terreno, licenças, acesso à rede, transformadores e quadros de distribuição, até mesmo grandes tornos para usinar eixos. "Se faltar qualquer coisa, por mais trivial que pareça, o poder de computação não funciona", escreveu ele. Alguns desses chips já estão esperando. No episódio de sexta-feira do podcast Moonshots de Peter Diamandis, o fundador da Link Ventures, Dave Blundin, disse que "há 15 gigawatts de chips ociosos porque não conseguem encontrar data centers que tenham resfriamento líquido." (Ele ainda acha que os chips serão o maior gargalo assim que a próxima onda de construção for concluída.) A conta de juros da CoreWeave não espera A CoreWeave tomou muito empréstimo para construir sua frota de GPUs da NVIDIA (NVDA). Sua dívida total no TIKR, que inclui obrigações de arrendamento, foi de $2 bilhões no final de 2023 para $29,8 bilhões no final de 2025… …e atingiu $51,6 bilhões até 30 de junho de 2026, incluindo $16,5 bilhões em arrendamentos. O negócio não gera receita suficiente para cobrir os juros dessa dívida. Em 2025, a CoreWeave pagou $1,2 bilhão de juros líquidos contra uma perda operacional de $46 milhões. A lacuna cresceu desde então. Os juros foram de $640 milhões apenas no segundo trimestre de 2026, contra uma perda operacional de $49 milhões, e a administração prevê de $860 milhões a $940 milhões para o terceiro trimestre. Locais inacabados já estão custando dinheiro. A CoreWeave capitalizou $176 milhões em juros sobre capacidade ainda em construção no primeiro semestre de 2026. E atrasos já a prejudicaram antes: em novembro de 2025, atrasos de um desenvolvedor de data center a forçaram a reduzir sua previsão de receita para 2025. Pagar pelo restante também está ficando mais difícil. O CEO da NVIDIA, Jensen Huang, disse à CNBC na semana passada que uma "escassez de capital" está prejudicando as construções das neoclouds. A Nebius também está gastando rápido A CoreWeave não é a única neocloud construindo antecipadamente. Os gastos de capital da Nebius foram de $82,9 milhões em 2023 para $808 milhões em 2024 e $4,07 bilhões em 2025. Nenhum desses gastos gera receita até que os locais para os quais estão indo tenham energia e resfriamento. Preços mais altos só pagam em chips conectados Os preços de aluguel estão ajudando o poder de computação que está em operação. A CoreWeave aumentou os preços cerca de 25% em todos os tipos de GPU em julho, e o amigo de Jin coloca os aluguéis de H100, B200 e B300 com alta de 2x a 3x. Mas um preço mais alto não paga nada em uma GPU que está esperando por um transformador. Em 21 de outubro, uma publicação no X chamou a demanda da SpaceX por poder de computação de otimista para as neoclouds. Musk respondeu: "Somente se conseguirem colocar seu poder de computação online e confiável, o que é extremamente difícil de fazer em escala." Os analistas não esperam que a receita operacional da CoreWeave cubra seus juros até 2028, quando o consenso projeta um EBIT de $8,8 bilhões contra $7,7 bilhões em juros. Um local paralisado só empurra isso mais para frente. A conclusão Musk está certo de que algum poder de computação ficará ocioso. A CoreWeave, com uma conta de juros maior que sua receita operacional, é quem carrega esse risco. Seus clientes tinham comprometido $104,2 bilhões de backlog até 30 de junho. Mas ela tinha apenas 1,5 gigawatt de potência ativa naquela época, contra 4,2 gigawatts contratados até 11 de agosto, e seu primeiro local de construção própria só entra em operação no final deste ano. A maior parte dessa lacuna depende de outras empresas concluírem seus prédios no prazo. Minha opinião: eu esperaria por provas de que a potência ativa da CoreWeave está alcançando seus contratos antes de comprar a ação. Claro, o relatório do terceiro trimestre de 12 de novembro poderia fornecer essa prova. A administração prevê uma receita operacional ajustada de $200 milhões a $260 milhões contra essa conta de jur

artigo.texto: SpaceX firma acordo de US$ 40 bilhões para financiar equipamentos de data centers A SpaceX, de Elon Musk, firmou um compromisso de financiamento de cerca de US$ 40 bilhões com uma entidade administrada pela Apollo Global Management para adquirir equipamentos destinados a centros de dados (data centers). Segundo documento enviado nesta segunda-feira, 26, à Securities and Exchanges Commission (SEC, a CVM dos EUA), a operação prevê o arrendamento de unidades de processamento gráfico (GPUs) e equipamentos relacionados. O compromisso vinculante foi assinado em 24 de outubro e estabelece que a entidade ligada à Apollo comprará os equipamentos e os alugará à SpaceX, que realizará pagamentos trimestrais ao longo de aproximadamente cinco anos. Os equipamentos serão entregues em lotes, com contratos individuais de arrendamento previstos para começar no primeiro semestre de 2027. Cada contrato terá duração de cinco anos a cinco anos e três meses. Segundo a companhia, os pagamentos trimestrais serão feitos antecipadamente e incluirão, em geral, um vigésimo do custo financiado de cada lote, além de juros calculados a uma taxa anual fixa sobre o saldo devedor e despesas adicionais. A taxa de juros ainda será definida. A SpaceX estima que os pagamentos de principal totalizem aproximadamente US$ 40 bilhões durante a vigência dos contratos, sem incluir juros e outros custos. A empresa espera concluir a formalização do acordo antes do fim de 2026, mediante o cumprimento de determinadas condições. Investimento em data center após balanço forte Na última semana, a SpaceX registrou um lucro líquido de US$ 4,4 bilhões no terceiro trimestre de 2026, em seu segundo relatório de lucros após a Oferta Pública Inicial (IPO, na sigla em inglês). O resultado ajustado por ação da SpaceX foi de US$ 0,35, acima das projeções de analistas compiladas pela FactSet, que projetavam lucro de US$ 0,13. A receita da empresa, por sua vez, subiu 161% na comparação anual, para US$ 14,6 bilhões, ante a estimativa de US$ 12,87 bilhões apurada pela FactSet junto a analistas. O segmento de conectividade, que consiste no serviço de internet via satélite Starlink, registrou 13,6 milhões de inscritos no terceiro trimestre deste ano e obteve receita de US$ 5,2 bilhões. Já os setores de Espaço e Inteligência Artificial (IA) registraram receita de US$ 1,77 bilhão e US$ 7,56 bilhões, respectivamente. artigo.texto: An inside look of the massive data center tearing a Wisconsin community apart In Port Washington, Wisconsin, there's a data center being built that's as big as 500 football fields. Residents aren't sure if it could save their community or destroy it. SACHA PFEIFFER, HOST: Back here in Wisconsin, I've been driving through the state this week. And just north of Milwaukee, you quickly enter farm country - cornfields, rolling hills, barns and grain silos. Then suddenly, next to a highway, you get a visual shock. And - oh, Henry, is this the data center on the left? HENRY LARSON, BYLINE: It's huge. PFEIFFER: There's something massive under construction over there. It's a hyper-scale data center in Port Washington, Wisconsin. I went there with NPR producer Henry Larson, and we could barely find words for how colossal this project is. This skyline of cranes and... It stretches along 2 miles of highway. It covers 2 1/2 million square feet of former farmland. LARSON: It goes literally to the horizon. PFEIFFER: This emerging data center complex has torn up the land and torn up this community. It's a local story playing out nationally as artificial intelligence companies race to build data centers to power their AI and many people increasingly say we don't want these here. (SOUNDBITE OF ARCHIVED RECORDING) UNIDENTIFIED PERSON #1: Will you acknowledge the mental health impacts of the residents living closest to the data center? Will you offer support to people who have endured the most? PFEIFFER: Port Washington's gargantuan project has led to angry protests, multiple lawsuits and opponents arrested for civil disobedience. Supporters say data centers will keep the United States competitive and could bring great wealth to places where they're built. But many residents feel frightened and helpless as they watch this rapid change, like 67-year-old Amanda Mueller. She relocated to Port Washington five years ago. AMANDA MUELLER: This was my last move. I feel like an elephant looking for a place to die in life, and I found utopia. It was so perfect. PFEIFFER: She bought a four-bedroom ranch house within walking distance of a beautiful, undeveloped stretch of beach on Lake Michigan. (SOUNDBITE OF FOOTSTEPS ON GRASS) PFEIFFER: Is this all your yard you see here, all this? MUELLER: Yeah. I own... PFEIFFER: Wow. MUELLER: ...Three acres. PFEIFFER: All the way to that fringe of... MUELLER: Yeah. PFEIFFER: ...Pine trees. MUELLER: Oh, all the way through there. PFEIFFER: Wow. MUELLER: This is the perfect retirement home. I mean... PFEIFFER: Look at this view you have. But her view is different this year. You can glimpse cranes in the distance. Port Washington's data center is being built about a half mile from her house. When did you get a hint that something was about to dramatically change in your neighborhood? MUELLER: I'm going to say two years ago. The farmer right next to me just sold a lot of his farmland. And then someone else said, yeah, another farmer's selling. And it's like, wait - it's all consolidated. PFEIFFER: Were you feeling some combination of kind of dread, dismay? MUELLER: I put my house up for sale. PFEIFFER: Literally? MUELLER: Yeah. PFEIFFER: But she says she got just one offer that eventually fell apart. She believes the buyer got spooked by the data center. Mueller is infuriated with the mayor and city council for approving this project. She's now one of Port Washington's leading crusaders against it, pushing back with litigation and asking for moratoriums and environmental reviews and more voter input. MUELLER: There should be a buffer zone around data centers, and it should be within at least a mile of a data center, you should not have residents living anywhere near it. There has to be guardrails. PFEIFFER: Port Washington Mayor Ted Neitzke says adequate guardrails have been put in place. There may be no bigger champion for this project than the mayor. (SOUNDBITE OF CAR DOOR CLOSING) TED NEITZKE: I don't know where you want me to start, but - so I'm 55. So I've lived here, went to high school here, married my wife, who's from here, our kids went to school here. PFEIFFER: He drives us around Port Washington, recalling when it was a declining industrial city that didn't yet have a cute touristy downtown. He thinks people against the data center have it all wrong, just like they were wrong about a popular brewery now located near the city's pretty marina. NEITZKE: So this is one of the new developments. This is where we'll go for beer and cheese curds. But this building here was very controversial. People lost their jobs on their council because this was a parking lot, and nobody wanted to lose the parking lot. Change is something that does not come easy to small Midwestern towns. PFEIFFER: In Port Washington, being mayor is a part-time job. It pays an annual stipend of $7,500. But the role gave Neitzke the power to help approve this $15 billion data center project. He envisions thousands of local jobs, beautification and infrastructure projects and a gusher of new tax revenue. NEITZKE: One of the things I did was I flew out to Loudoun County, Virginia, and I went and visited all the data centers... PFEIFFER: One of the epicenters... NEITZKE: Yeah. PFEIFFER: ...Of data centers. NEITZKE: I mean, I don't know if you can find more in the United States. And as I drove around, I really could not understand - what are people so mad about? Because when you're in that area, and you're driving around, they're just large boxes filled with computers. PFEIFFER: But you really can't imagine what people would be mad about? NEITZKE: Honestly, if you did your diligence, I don't understand why a community like ours, who grew up an industrial base, would fight the fact that we would need this back again. artigo.texto: Watson Farley & Williams (WFW) has advised BNP Paribas Asset Management, Santander, Banco Sabadell, and Banco Cooperativo Español, acting as lenders, on the €222 million financing of a portfolio of hybrid solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage system (BESS) projects in Spain owned by BRUC Alter Energías Renovables, S.A., a joint venture owned by BRUC and Alter Enersun. The financing combines the financing of an operational 208 MW PV portfolio with the financing for the construction of 118 MW/472 MWh of co-located BESS capacity across four projects in Extremadura and Andalucía, Spain. This creates an integrated renewable generation and storage portfolio designed to optimise the management and distribution of renewable electricity. The transaction forms part of BRUC and Alter Enersun’s strategy to further integrate renewable generation and energy storage, reinforcing the growing role of hybrid renewable projects in Spain’s energy transition. The addition of battery storage capacity enables the storage of the electricity generated by the PV plants and facilitate its dispatch according to system requirements, providing greater flexibility to renewable generation. BRUC is a leading independent renewable energy platform in the Iberian market, with a diversified portfolio of renewable generation assets. Alter Enersun is a leading Iberian renewable energy company with PV installations across Spain, Portugal, and Italy. The WFW Madrid Energy team that advised the lenders was led by Finance Partner, José María Anarte, supported by Senior Associate, Antón Ramil, and Associate, Sara Estradera. José María commented: “This transaction highlights the growing convergence of renewable generation and energy storage in Spain’s energy market. The financing of a portfolio combining operating PV assets and large scale battery storage reflects the increasing sophistication of the country’s renewable energy sector and the evolution of financing structures required to support it. We are delighted to have advised the lenders on a landmark transaction at the forefront of this trend, an area in which WFW continues to play a leading role.” For more news and technical articles from the global renewable industry, read the latest issue of Energy Global magazine. artigo.texto: POTTERVILLE — U.S. Rep. Tom Barrett is pushing legislation to increase transparency around data center projects and protect local control over their development, alongside health insurance reforms and limits on presidential war powers as he seeks a second term. The Livingston Post and its partner, Michigan Firsthand, caught up with the Republican congressman as he went door-to-door in the Potterville neighborhood near the first home he bought after returning from an Iraq deployment. In the wide-ranging interview, Barrett — who faces Democratic challenger William Lawrence in the Nov. 3 election for Michigan’s 7th Congressional District — also discussed inflation, artificial intelligence, Israel, education and public safety. (You can watch the full discussions with Barrett and Lawrence on YouTube, and read our companion interview with Lawrence here.) Acknowledging the high stakes – the race is the nation’s costliest House race for advertising according to WKAR and AdImpact – Barrett said he is feeling “optimistic.” “I’ve been in tough political campaigns before, and I know what it feels like to be in a close race,” he said. Local control of data centers Barrett said data center decisions should rest with local townships, villages and cities, and that residents should have the right to examine proposals before agreements are signed. On Aug. 20, Barrett introduced legislation to protect state and local authority over data center siting. On Sept. 24, he joined Maryland Democratic Rep. Jamie Raskin in co-sponsoring Ohio Democratic Rep. Greg Landsman’s No Secrets for Data Centers Act, which would make covered nondisclosure agreements unenforceable. “I don’t want to do a ban on the development of AI or a ban on data centers entirely,” Barrett said, saying he was concerned about rising electricity costs, water consumption, noise and what communities would do with large facilities if technological changes ever made them obsolete. “What I want to make sure is that any data center project is done with the consent of the residents who live there.” Barrett said some communities may conclude a proposal meets their needs, while others may reject it. He argued that transparency requirements would not undermine the United States’ ability to compete in artificial intelligence, saying “if we’re going to do this, we’re going to do it with transparency and in the right way that addresses the concerns that people have.” Keeping humans in control of AI The 22-year Army veteran, who served in Iraq, Guantanamo Bay and South Korea, also supports pursuing an international agreement governing artificial intelligence and autonomous weapons. “I think every country should agree that having fully autonomous lethal weapons is dangerous in so many different ways,” he said. Barrett joined Democratic Reps. Don Beyer of Virginia and Sara Jacobs of California in introducing the Human Authority over Autonomous Weapons Act, which would require meaningful human oversight of intentionally lethal strikes by autonomous or AI-enabled weapons used by the U.S. military. He said the possibility that terrorist groups could obtain such weapons should give countries a common interest in negotiating limits. “I can’t say with certainty that they would, but I can say that I believe that it’s the appropriate thing to do,” he said. Health care reform and private insurance On health care, Barrett called for substantial changes to the healthcare system, including requiring insurers to spend more of their premium revenue on patient care, and expanding access to tax-exempt health savings accounts. “So I agree that the healthcare system in the country is broken, and we need substantial, radical reform,” he said. “I’ve actually introduced legislation that would increase what’s called the medical loss ratio.” His Care Over Profits Act would require insurers to spend at least 85% of premium revenue on medical care and quality improvement. Barrett said he also wants broader access to health savings accounts and expanded eligible expenses, including healthy food, gym memberships and fitness equipment. He argued that allowing workers and employers to contribute to accounts that follow people between jobs would give families more control over their coverage and encourage preventive care. “These big health insurance companies have gotten by on raising premiums and not increasing quality of care,” he said. Barrett rejected the Medicare for All approach, arguing that eliminating the commercial insurance market could undermine medical innovation and reduce the revenue hospitals and physicians rely on. “Today, the Medicare system works because we have a robust commercial insurance program as well,” he said. He said providers depend on a mix of patients with commercial insurance, Medicare and Medicaid, and warned that moving everyone to government payment rates could affect services. Iran, affordability and congressional authority In between conversations with voters, Barrett said people frequently have concerns about gasoline and diesel prices, and the effects on groceries, deliveries and agriculture. He blamed today’s inflationary environment on spending during the Biden administration, and acknowledged the Iran war is helping drive fuel-price increases. Ending the conflict, he said, would help stabilize costs. In April, Barrett introduced the bipartisan Prevent Endless Wars Act with Democratic Rep. Jared Golden of Maine, a measure that would deny expedited congressional consideration to military-force authorizations lasting more than five years or lacking an expiration date. “Our Constitution makes it clear that only Congress can decide to send our men and women into combat or not,” he said.
